Today, the only frequently debated topic is whether or not to conserve energy and resources, since some businesses have adopted a four-day work week with each day consisting of ten hours. Should your school follow this model by extending the school day by two hours? Some people think that extending the school day will not conserve energy and resources. They feel that the extra time in school is the same thing and that it will result in higher spending on energy—such as electricity, lights, computer charges, electric blackboards, and more—and that water usage will increase because some students forget to close the washstand in the bathroom. I believe that the school should extend the day by two hours because we must take care to conserve energy and resources, and, last but not least, we will have more time to make the world better and build conscience.

One reason I believe that the school should follow this model by extending the school day by two hours is that we can conserve more energy for the future. Also, the school should instruct each student on how to consume energy carefully—for example, by teaching which light is correct for use at home and giving tips that may help them pay the least possible electricity bill.

Another reason is that I feel water is a resource we can save in the school because all students use the bathroom almost twice and often forget to pull down the toilet handle. I think the students can make posters to show the importance of saving water and other resources such as plastic and paper, because in some places these resources are purchased with money that could make the school better than others, and the students should be more careful with them.

The final reason is that I believe if the school adds two hours per day, students and teachers will have more time to do more things. One idea is that they could create a propaganda campaign to show society how to prevent global climate change and instruct people on how to take care of the world; another is to develop an online page to instruct students and others outside the school on how to be careful.

As you have read, I think that the school should add two hours per day because everyone in the school can become more conscious about saving energy and resources and, ultimately, help the world. Only when we gain the conscience to change the world will we have a better world one day.

There is an ongoing discussion about whether extending the school day by two hours can help conserve energy and resources, especially since some businesses have adopted a four-day work week with longer hours. Some argue that keeping students at school longer will not save energy at all; in fact, they claim that it leads to higher electricity costs due to additional computer usage, lighting, and other facilities. I, however, believe that a longer school day can encourage energy and resource conservation while also giving us more time to work on making the world a better place.

One main point in favor of a two-hour extension is that it can help save energy for future needs. A longer school day provides an opportunity for schools to educate students on the proper ways to manage energy use at home. For instance, teachers can demonstrate how to choose energy-efficient light bulbs and share practical methods to reduce electricity bills.

Another important advantage is conserving water. Since students tend to use restrooms multiple times and sometimes forget to turn off the taps, longer school hours could be a chance to increase awareness about using water wisely. Encouraging students to create posters about water conservation, as well as reducing unnecessary use of paper and plastic within the school, could lead to significant savings. These practices could also free up funds that might be used to improve the school's facilities, making it a better learning environment.

Lastly, extending the school day would offer more time for educational and social initiatives that benefit the community. Both teachers and students could work together on projects, such as a campaign promoting awareness about global climate change and sustainable practices. They might even develop an online platform to share tips on how to conserve energy and resources, thereby extending the impact beyond the school itself.

In summary, I strongly support the idea of adding two extra hours to the school day. Not only does this change encourage responsible use of energy and resources, but it also serves as a valuable opportunity to educate and inspire students to become more conscientious citizens. Only when we all become aware of our impact on the world can we hope to create lasting improvements for the future.

Online classes are a very practical option for many students, especially those balancing work and family responsibilities. When work schedules do not align with traditional school hours, studying from home can be a lifesaver. After a long day at work, students might find it easier to attend lessons online because they can study in a relaxed environment, take breaks when needed, and even grab a bite to eat before diving into their studies.

Furthermore, online education helps address issues related to illness and transportation. For instance, if a student is feeling unwell, attending a virtual class minimizes the risk of spreading an infection to peers. Not everyone has access to a car or convenient parking, and unpredictable weather can sometimes make travel difficult. In these situations, being able to log in from home provides a much-needed solution.

Another advantage of remote learning is its flexibility for those with family responsibilities. Students who are parents or caretakers can more easily manage their time when they do not have to leave the house. This flexibility is also beneficial for students who face mobility challenges, as it removes the barriers associated with commuting to a physical campus. In turn, they can remain engaged in their education without added stress.

Ultimately, technology simplifies many aspects of life by offering timely solutions that fit busy schedules. Online classes enable students to balance work, health, and family needs effectively, ensuring that learning remains accessible and manageable regardless of the obstacles they may face.

Imagine a school where every student is required to take part in a physical activity ordered by the principal. This arrangement might seem fair at first, but it overlooks the fact that many children need time to relax and pursue hobbies they truly enjoy. For some students, mandatory activities can cause unnecessary stress, especially when they need to recharge after a long day of academic work.

Students have busy schedules filled with homework and other responsibilities. They require adequate downtime to maintain their energy and overall well-being. When they are forced to participate, they lose valuable moments that could be spent socializing or simply resting. For instance, chatting with friends and relaxing are activities that help them prepare for more demanding tasks later. These quiet moments are just as important as any structured exercise.

Moreover, many children prefer indoor leisure activities such as playing video games or reading rather than engaging in outdoor exercises. Some students find comfort in being at home, enjoying activities they love without the pressure of organized tasks. Forcing them to take part in school activities can interfere with their personal interests and decrease their motivation.

In my opinion, mandating a set activity for everyone is not ideal. If I were the principal, I would allow students the freedom to choose whether to participate, join a club, or simply enjoy some quiet time indoors.

Have you ever experienced repeated failure until you finally mastered a challenging skill? I firmly believe that setbacks are a crucial part of reaching success. For instance, I once knew a young athlete who struggled to catch a football—it constantly slipped from his hands. Over time, with persistent practice, he learned to secure the ball at just the right moment. This example shows that practicing a skill, no matter how difficult it seems at first, is essential if you want to improve. 

Failure is not just a step towards success but also a natural part of life. Every setback offers an opportunity to learn and grow, provided you are willing to get up and try again. Without failing, you might never understand the true meaning of success. Although some individuals appear to be naturally talented, it is important to remember that no one becomes proficient on their very first attempt. 

I encourage everyone to challenge themselves by working on skills they are not yet good at, even if it means failing repeatedly for a while. After a month of consistent practice, you might be surprised by how much you improve. Embracing failure as a stepping stone can be the key to achieving your goals and ultimately finding success.

When we're born, we come out of our mother's womb. The first thing we naturally do is screech and cry; if we don't cry, the doctor hits us on our back to try to make us cry. From that moment onward, we develop our own distinct sound and screech with its unique pitch. They take our fingerprints, ensuring that no two are the same—even when we are born with a twin, the prints will never be identical. From that point, we begin to learn and develop our own persona.

After we're born, our brain starts to function with even the smallest stimuli. Babies learn to cry when they're hungry, need changing, are in pain, or simply seek attention. As children enter the toddler stage, they begin to learn how to walk by observing others, and they learn to talk by listening to everyone around them. We learn how to grab our bottle, pick up a fork or spoon, and carry out our daily activities. All of this is learned from observing and listening to others.

When we reach the age of 6 to 12, we tend to want to fit in with the cool kids by watching TV and seeing celebrities, musicians, actors, painters, policemen, firemen, dentists, doctors, mayors, chefs, and various athletes such as soccer players, basketball players, football players, baseball players, hockey players, tennis players, and volleyball players. The list could go on indefinitely, but the point is that we are influenced by these examples.

As we enter our teen years (13–19), we begin to develop our own voice—at least until we are old enough to truly own it. We each take our own paths and make our own decisions. Our parents no longer accompany us throughout the day to tell us what to do, although they offer strong advice because they have already been through that stage and do not want to see us fail or get hurt. Sometimes, however, it is beneficial to fail and make mistakes because then we learn what we can or cannot do.

Now, as you become an adult, the safety net we once had under our parents' roof is gone; we no longer have that privilege and must grow up to officially create and develop our own persona. When you get a job, it comes with responsibilities and teaches you whether you are responsible or irresponsible, social or non-social, lenient or strict, patient or impatient, forgiving or unforgiving.

I’d like to think that we are all born to grow and learn about our rugged society. Our experiences shape how we behave. For example, we can literally live in a dire situation and still maintain the happiest attitude—perhaps even a better one than a boy or girl who complains about not getting the car they wanted. This contrasts with the kid who witnessed his mother being beaten by his deadbeat dad, the kid who spent the night wondering if his mom would come home, or the child who went to bed hungry.

So, honestly, I don't think we're born with labels. I feel that we can all make our own decisions about what we will make of life instead of sitting idly and allowing everyone to perceive us with pity. A significant factor in your character is your mentality: if you have a broken, weak mindset, you will exude negative vibes and possess a deadbeat character, but if you have a strong mindset and the will to get things done, you'll develop a broad and respected character. In conclusion, I'd like to think that we create and build our own character and that no higher power assigns us a label for who we are destined to be.

From the moment we are born, we enter the world by crying—a sound so essential that even doctors sometimes encourage it by tapping our backs. From this first sound, we begin developing unique traits like our voice, which carries its own pitch and character. Alongside our first cry, our fingerprints are taken, each set completely distinct, even between twins who share every other similarity.

As we grow up, our brains begin to take in information from the world. In infancy, we learn to cry when we are hungry, uncomfortable, or in need of comfort. As toddlers, we observe those around us to learn vital skills like walking, speaking, and handling everyday objects, such as bottles or utensils. Watching and listening to others is our first lesson in how to live.

During our childhood years, roughly between ages six and twelve, our desire to fit in often guides us. This is when we absorb influences from television, celebrities, and a wide range of professions—from musicians and actors to doctors, firemen, and athletes. Clearly, we are deeply affected by the examples set by others.

Entering the teenage years, roughly between thirteen and nineteen, we start finding our own voice. It is a time when we begin to make our own decisions. While our parents offer advice from their past experiences to protect us from mistakes, there is also value in failing and learning from our own errors. This period represents a shift where we begin to shape our individual identities.

Adulthood brings a new landscape of responsibility. Without the protective net of our childhood home, we are pushed to develop our own character. Gaining employment and managing responsibilities teaches us whether we are reliable or careless, sociable or reserved, patient or impulsive, forgiving or resentful. I believe that our life experiences mold who we are. Some people, even in difficult circumstances, remain positive, while others might dwell on smaller disappointments.

Ultimately, I see that we are not born with fixed labels. Instead, through our decisions and actions, we build and define our own character. Whether one has a resilient mindset or not, the choices made throughout life have a profound impact on who we become.

Technology’s impact on human contact can be seen from both positive and negative perspectives, depending largely on an individual’s situation. On one hand, technology offers significant benefits by helping those who often feel lonely. For many, having access to a variety of activities such as reading, playing games, shopping online, or watching shows on platforms like Netflix and YouTube can provide comfort and distractions from the feelings of isolation. These applications not only entertain but also offer a way to connect with the world. It is important to remember that feeling alone can be very damaging to one’s mental well-being, and in some cases, people might even choose immersive virtual experiences over life’s harsher realities, such as confronting unemployment or other difficulties.

Despite these advantages, technology also brings drawbacks that affect our social interactions. The ease of communication through smartphones and computers may reduce the desire to engage in face-to-face conversations. Nowadays, many people seem disinterested in traditional gatherings, such as family reunions, instead preferring the company of online friends or solitary digital interactions. It is not unusual to listen to someone speak while they remain preoccupied with their phone, sending a message or browsing social media, which can make the speaker feel dismissed and unimportant. This behavior may eventually lead to a decline in genuine relationships and could foster an environment where people feel increasingly isolated despite being constantly connected online.

Furthermore, while technology simplifies everyday tasks such as shopping or ordering food, it inadvertently encourages a more sedentary lifestyle. With everything available at the tap of a screen, some individuals might ask themselves why they should make an effort in the real world when their devices are capable of handling so many tasks. This reliance might hinder the development of important social skills and reduce the appeal of direct human interaction over time.

In conclusion, technology is an incredible tool that can greatly enrich our lives when used appropriately. However, it is crucial to strike a balance in its use so that it enhances rather than replaces meaningful human connections. Both the benefits and downsides of technology remind us that while it makes life easier, maintaining real, personal interactions remains essential for our well-being.

Self-reliance means having the ability to make decisions on our own and to think for ourselves rather than simply following others. Facing problems requires us to ask questions, share ideas, and gather diverse perspectives in order to create better solutions.

Teaching young people to think independently, rather than simply following commands, lays the foundation for leadership. Even leaders start small; they build their knowledge bit by bit, always looking for more information through questions and discussions. This continual search for guidance not only strengthens our personal careers but also positively influences our communities and families.

When individuals stand up for what they believe is right and seek input from others, they open up a wider array of choices and insights. A clear example of self-reliance is seen in the military, where the lives of service members depend on their ability to act and decide quickly. Soldiers undergo rigorous training that prepares them not only physically but mentally, so they can make critical decisions without hesitation when every moment counts. This readiness, built on individual responsibility and continuous learning, mirrors the everyday decisions we must all make when it comes to our careers, families, and future plans.

Regardless of our age, background, or any other label, developing self-reliance and seeking advice are skills that serve us well in the long term. Technology plays a vital role in our everyday lives by providing assistance in various aspects such as communication, entertainment, and problem-solving. In recent years, technological advancements have progressed rapidly. Nowadays, devices like smartphones, tablets, and computers allow us to access global news instantly, connect with family and friends, and keep up with classmates—all at our fingertips.

Its positive impact on society is evident in many ways. Technology simplifies shopping, offers endless entertainment through games and music, and provides access to countless applications. Tools like GPS for navigation, online translators, and digital libraries have become essential, often available to everyone at little or no cost.

One major benefit is the everyday help technology offers. For instance, if someone finds themselves lost, GPS on a mobile device can guide them to their intended location, whether it’s a store, supermarket, or any other destination. This feature illustrates how beneficial technology can be in unexpected situations.

Furthermore, technology serves as a source of entertainment. When boredom strikes, people can listen to music from various genres, play downloadable games, or read books available digitally. In just a few keystrokes or through a simple search, a mobile device can present multiple options, showing how easily entertainment is accessible compared to traditional outlets such as bookstores.

Communication has also been revolutionized by technology. Today, applications like Facebook, WhatsApp, Instagram, and Messenger make it effortless for people to connect regardless of distance. These platforms help maintain close ties with family and childhood friends by allowing sharing of photos and videos, thereby strengthening personal bonds while keeping the world at our fingertips.

In addition, when facing challenges such as cooking difficulties, vehicle issues, or home repairs, technology provides valuable guidance. Online platforms like Google and YouTube offer detailed tutorials and step-by-step videos that assist in finding practical solutions. This online assistance helps individuals gain knowledge and resolve issues even if professional help is not immediately available.

Moreover, technology plays an important role in job hunting. Many companies prefer online applications, making it simple to apply for a job using a computer, smartphone, or tablet. The internet also helps businesses promote their products and services globally, enabling them to expand quickly and become internationally recognized, consequently increasing their profits.

In summary, technology is an indispensable tool that greatly enhances our lives. It not only facilitates communication and entertainment but also aids in problem-solving and job searching. With endless applications available—from navigation to social media—technology helps bridge distances and brings people together, proving that it was designed to support and develop human connections in our increasingly interconnected world.

Ralph Waldo Emerson once stated, "Unless you try to do something beyond what you already know, you will never grow." I fully agree with his view, and I believe there are several reasons to support this idea.

Secondly, having a broad array of knowledge can provide a clear advantage over others. Knowledge is a powerful asset that cannot simply be bought; it must be earned through learning and experience. When individuals take on challenges beyond their comfort zones, they not only gain new insights but also increase their capacity to solve problems and contribute in different ways. For example, a university graduate who ventures into more challenging areas after obtaining a degree in teaching may find themselves advancing to higher positions such as school administration or leadership roles.

In conclusion, I strongly agree with Emerson’s statement. By continually seeking challenges beyond what we already know, we open ourselves up to growth, new opportunities, and more fulfilling lives.

My uncle had 100 dollars in his wallet; he handed me 10 dollars and kept the remainder. I suggested that he save the money for later, as he might need it soon, but he chose to spend it all on shirts, pants, and hats. The next day, he found himself asking for money for gas. He was happy with his purchases even though he had been aware that the money was needed for the following day.

Considering several opinions can lead to better decisions. For example, one friend wanted to spend his money to see a movie in the cinema, despite us suggesting otherwise because the movie was already available on DVD for much less money. When he listened to our viewpoints, he saw the situation from a different angle and realized that paying more for a theater experience wasn’t the best idea.

Additionally, when seeking advice from multiple people, it can help highlight potential pitfalls. My dad once gave me money to buy whatever I wanted, knowing I would eventually need a white shirt. I decided to purchase a game instead, and the very next day, when we needed the shirt, I was out of funds. My dad reminded me that he had advised me to save the money, and it was a lesson in the importance of listening and planning ahead.

In summary, these experiences underscore the importance of listening to those around you, as multiple perspectives can help you avoid unnecessary spending and be better prepared for upcoming needs.

Online classes and video conferencing serve as invaluable resources for both students unable to afford traditional college expenses and adults who have been hindered by financial restraints from pursuing further education. With escalating living costs and campus fees, many students face the burden of additional expenses, which forces them to work extra hours on top of their studies. This balancing act between earning a living and keeping up with academic responsibilities often results in increased stress and a more complicated daily routine.

Another significant concern is the challenge of commuting and finding parking. Many students opt for online classes because it eliminates the need to rush to campus, find parking spaces, or deal with the delays of public transport. For institutions with sprawling campuses, parking availability can be limited. Moreover, not every student has access to a personal vehicle, making online learning an attractive alternative that saves time and alleviates many logistical issues.

Studying from home also offers students a more focused learning environment. Without the distractions commonly associated with traditional classroom settings, they can absorb lessons more effectively and manage their time efficiently. In a virtual setting, students have the opportunity to review lectures and ask questions whenever necessary, which can lead to a deeper understanding of the subject matter. Additionally, instructors often streamline assignments for online learners, which helps maintain a balanced workload and allows students more flexibility to manage their academic and personal commitments.

In summary, online education and video conferencing not only provide a viable solution for those facing financial and transportation challenges but also promote a more organized and efficient learning experience. This mode of education enables students to meet their academic goals while still managing other aspects of their lives, ultimately opening up opportunities for those who might otherwise be left behind.

I believe that success in life begins with making things easier for yourself by showing that you are unique and kind, regardless of what others might think or say. It is essential to stay calm when facing difficulties and to approach problems with a positive attitude. Getting angry seldom leads to good results, so treating others well, maintaining inner peace, and cultivating strong relationships with those around you are crucial steps in building a successful life. A cheerful and composed demeanor when facing life's challenges makes all the difference.

When you are genuinely kind to others, both you and the people around you benefit. Kindness sets you apart in a world where many seem indifferent or even hostile. Despite encountering individuals with a negative attitude, it is important not to abandon your own values. Instead, surround yourself with those who share your positive outlook. For instance, I enjoy deep friendships with my family and friends because I take the time to understand their interests and values. Their support reinforces my belief that maintaining a good and caring demeanor leads to better opportunities and success in the long run.

Inner peace is another vital element for a fulfilling life. The sense of calm that comes from within provides comfort and strength, even when faced with uncomfortable or challenging situations. Although it can be hard to achieve, finding activities that you love and that keep you engaged can help maintain this peace. I have learned from personal experience that holding on to negative feelings, like the grudge I had since my younger brother upset me when I was twelve, only makes life more difficult. Over time, focusing on our bond and communicating openly has helped me preserve my inner peace and appreciate the closeness we share.

Building strong, positive connections with others also plays an important role in nurturing a constructive mindset. When you spend time with people who focus on the positive and share helpful ideas, they can significantly influence your future. It is important to be cautious, though, because not everyone will push you towards success. I have seen a friend whose academic performance declined after he started spending time with people who did not share the same ambition. His gradual shift away from his previous hardworking nature is a reminder that surrounding yourself with supportive, motivated individuals is essential for long-term success.

Ultimately, being kind to everyone, nurturing inner peace, and connecting with positive people are the pillars of a successful life. These principles remind us that maintaining a good attitude, regardless of the issues we face, is key to moving forward and achieving happiness and success.

In some societies, students are expected to identify a career by the time they enter high school. People who start a career can make it happen. Students who took it early can ask their counsler for advices. Many students believe that starting a career at a young age is a good idea because students can go to college after their courses, students can get a job after college, and students doesn't have to worry about making one in the future. Starting a career at a young age is a bad idea because it can cause students to quit their courses, it can cause lots of thinking to make one, and it can cause waste of time.

Students will quit their courses. For instance, when ever they went to class and took it for three weeks, they will usually give up. Furthermore, it can cause people to lose interest about their career. Teens who quit their courses, they have a hard time because it was difficult for them to keep up. Therefore, it is important to think first before taking that class.

It can cause lots of thinking to make one. For example, it takes time for adults to make their career. In addition, they will mostly think about getting a job first. Adults will usually think about getting a job because they want to earn money first. Not only that, adults like to spend time with their friends, but they make their career after they get paid enough to start their life.

It can cause waste of time. In fact, kids will spend time playing video games than making a career. Moreover, they think that career is school related. When making a career, kids will often write "don't know" and they will usually get back to their hobby. Thus, it is essintial to make a plan first before making a career at a young age.

Making a career at age of twelve or under is careless because it made people over think, it made them go back doing something, and it can cause them negative towards their courses. When ever they took their class about two ore three weeks, they usually will give up. Kids will often write "don't know" on their career paper. Making a career will take time for people to make, but don't give up easily if they can't pace up.

In some cultures, it is expected that students choose a career path by the time they reach high school. This early decision is meant to set students on a clear route toward further education and eventual employment. Supporters believe that beginning career planning at a young age offers several benefits: students can pursue higher education directly after completing their courses, secure a job following college, and avoid the stress of making career decisions later in life. However, starting a career too early can have significant drawbacks, such as interrupting education, leading to overthinking about future plans, and wasting valuable time.

Firstly, students may abandon their courses prematurely. For example, after attending classes consistently for a few weeks, many students become discouraged and give up. This lack of persistence often results in a diminished interest in pursuing a meaningful career path, leaving teenagers unprepared and struggling to catch up later.

Secondly, early career decisions can force individuals into excessive contemplation over their future. Adults often spend considerable time weighing their options and planning their careers, primarily because they need to secure a job to earn money. Balancing work, personal life, and career planning is challenging, and making such decisions at a young age can add undue pressure.

Lastly, trying to establish a career at a very young age may lead to inefficient use of time. Many young people might find themselves spending more hours on leisure activities, such as playing video games, rather than focusing on career planning. Often, when asked about their future plans, students write “don’t know,” indicating that they prefer to engage in hobbies over making significant career choices without a proper plan.

In conclusion, deciding on a career path before reaching high school can be unwise, as it may disrupt education, lead to overthinking, and result in wasted time. Young individuals might easily give up after a few weeks of trying, showing a trend of uncertainty toward their chosen career path. It is important to plan carefully and allow time for growth before making such an important decision.

By starting modestly, you create opportunities to learn from small setbacks, gradually building confidence and capability. Each mistake becomes a stepping stone that strengthens your character and prepares you for greater responsibilities in the future.

On the other hand, aiming too high from the very beginning may lead to overlooking the necessary effort and planning. Someone who rushes into big challenges without thoughtful preparation risks losing everything with just one misstep. By choosing a lower starting point, you can take a measured, step-by-step approach that minimizes risk and maximizes learning along the way.

Lower goals help protect what you have worked hard to achieve. This approach provides time to consider every decision carefully, ensuring steady progress without overwhelming setbacks. While it is beneficial to challenge oneself occasionally, it is important to do so without risking everything at once.

In my opinion, taking a moment to think before acting is essential for long-term success. A careful, measured approach allows you to build a solid foundation for reaching higher goals in the future while avoiding unnecessary losses.

To improve and experience personal growth, one must set small, achievable goals that eventually lead to larger accomplishments. Despite the inherent difficulties that come with learning and perfecting new skills, having confidence in your abilities is key to becoming truly proficient.

Think of it this way: if you already know how to ride a bicycle, why not try riding a motorcycle? If you have baked a cupcake before, you're ready to tackle a full cake. Even if you can float in water, learning to swim opens up a host of new opportunities. These incremental challenges refine and enhance your existing skills, allowing you to reach heights and achieve tasks that once seemed unattainable. Pushing yourself outside of your comfort zone is essential; without that drive, none of your goals can be met. Ultimately, the choice is yours—either to embrace personal growth through perseverance or to remain stagnant and miss out on future achievements.

I support the idea of setting a curfew for teenagers because it can help keep them from getting into trouble. Some teenagers remain out late and tend to disturb others, so requiring them to be home by 10 P.M. seems sensible. Although many young people are focused on their studies and need rest for school the next day, the curfew is designed to reduce the negative behaviors seen on the streets.

Too many teenagers find themselves in trouble because of activities they shouldn’t be involved in. In some instances, they carry weapons even though they are underage, and others get mixed up in dangerous situations simply by being with peers who do. Overall, I believe that a 10 P.M. curfew for teenagers is a good idea, as it would help keep them safe and reduce disturbances in our community.

Technology is now an integral part of everyday life, influencing how we work, learn, and communicate. Although some critics claim that it reduces the need for personal interaction, I believe that technology brings more positive effects when used appropriately. People rely on technology to access information and opportunities that would not be available otherwise, making our lives easier and more efficient.

In many professional fields, technology plays a vital role. For instance, numerous jobs depend entirely on digital tools that help workers solve problems independently, creating opportunities to earn a living. In the field of education, both students and teachers benefit greatly from technological devices. Students often complete assignments using computers, and teachers increasingly rely on online resources to share information. In the United States, it is common to see a significant shift from traditional textbooks to digital tools, which assist in finding quick answers and promote a more interactive learning environment.

Moreover, improvements in healthcare highlight the benefits of modern technology. Medical professionals now use advanced devices in operations, resulting in safer procedures and saving more lives compared to earlier times when they depended solely on textbooks and traditional methods. Although technology has simplified many aspects of our lives, it has sometimes been misapplied, such as in factories where over-reliance on automated machinery reduces the need for human labor.

On the other hand, there are valid concerns about the reduction of face-to-face communication. In some Latin American communities, for example, technology has even been dubbed the “new babysitter,” as parents use devices to keep children occupied while they attend to other tasks. Additionally, some individuals exploit digital platforms for harmful purposes like fraud, cyber theft, and other criminal activities. Such instances serve as a reminder that while most people use technology for beneficial outcomes, there are those who choose to misuse it for their own gain.

To sum up, despite its potential to limit direct human interaction, technology has largely enhanced our way of living by advancing education, work, and healthcare. Both digital communication and personal encounters have their own benefits and drawbacks, and the key is to strike a balance between the two. Ultimately, we should continue to embrace technology while also keeping the importance of personal, human connection in mind.

I strongly believe in always telling the truth because by doing so I demonstrate sincerity and avoid deceiving anyone. Being truthful means that people feel confident in asking for my help or sharing their own struggles, regardless of whether others are as transparent or not. I place honesty at the core of my character, as I see it as an essential trait that strengthens with time and experience. Moreover, I feel that by being honest, I create a foundation that minimizes potential setbacks like academic failure or being mistreated by peers.

However, there are times when complete honesty might lead to complications. If I share the truth and someone becomes upset because of it, they may lose trust in me permanently. It would be disheartening to compromise my integrity merely to please a friend or family member, only to see negative outcomes occur—even if those outcomes are unlikely. A damaged relationship might result, where my honesty is doubted, and they might value wisdom from someone else instead. Over time, the person might eventually realize their error and seek forgiveness, which could restore faith in my sincerity, but the process remains painful.

In situations of disagreement, instead of sparking intense conflict, I believe it is best to calmly discuss our differences face to face. Such discussions are less likely to harm anyone’s feelings and prevent long-lasting estrangements. In a broader sense, surrounding myself with others who prioritize honesty can help reduce negativity and stress, ensuring that we focus on uplifting our relationships rather than dwelling on past faults.

Even if someone claims they cannot rely on my honesty, I remain unaffected by thoughts of failure. I am committed to standing by my truthful nature, regardless of any temporary lapses or misunderstandings. For example, when I face a challenging test, I reassure myself that I will do my best to succeed. If I do poorly because I did not prepare adequately, I recognize that it was my own oversight rather than a failure of honesty. When truly needed, I will always draw on my commitment to truth to overcome difficulties and avoid becoming a failure.

I wish for everyone to embrace honesty as a fundamental trait because it is a powerful tool for resolving conflicts gradually rather than by force. Many people argue that honesty is not their top value until they fully understand its benefits. While some assume that highly intelligent people exhibit better honesty, I believe that integrity is not confined to intelligence; anyone, regardless of their mental capacity, can grow and eventually exhibit profound honesty over time. Even those who seem clever today may lose their integrity if they are not continually reminded of the value of truth. Family members and educators play an important role in guiding anyone who might be straying from honest behavior, just as friends sometimes distract us from it.

In the end, as people observe positive changes in someone who has always strived to be honest, they may be inspired and even share that transformation with others. That is why I see truthfulness as the most essential quality in life—it not only strengthens personal relationships but also builds a more trustworthy environment for everyone.

One frequently debated issue is whether students should determine their future career path by the time they enter high school. Many believe that the high school curriculum should steer students toward a specific profession, but I disagree with this idea. At such a young age, students generally lack the life experience and maturity necessary to make an informed career decision.

A primary concern is that teenagers simply do not possess enough knowledge or exposure to various fields to select a definite career. During high school, students are still in the process of exploring different interests and developing a clearer sense of what they might want to pursue professionally. Consequently, expecting them to commit to a particular career too early can limit their future opportunities.

Furthermore, making a career choice at a young age can lead to hasty decisions. Teenagers may later discover that their initial choice does not suit their evolving interests or abilities. For instance, one of my friends opted for a technology class during his freshman year after researching potential incomes, but he eventually found that the field did not meet his expectations. As a result, he switched to a materials and process class, which better aligned with his desire to learn practical skills like construction.

In my view, the best approach for high school students is to concentrate on academics and explore a wide range of subjects until they gain more insight into their personal interests and abilities. Waiting until later in high school or even college allows for a more measured decision-making process when it comes to choosing courses and planning a career path.

Overall, I believe that keeping an open mind and gathering as much experience as possible during high school is more beneficial than committing to a specific career at a young age. This strategy not only fosters academic success but also prepares students for a more informed and thoughtful decision-making process in the future.

I believe that students can greatly benefit from the option of attending classes from home. Studying remotely may help them feel more prepared and focused, resulting in a better learning experience. One advantage of this method is that it reduces the pressure of facing negative comments or judgment from peers. Often, students hear remarks like, "You’re not good enough" or "Your English isn’t great," which can hold them back in a traditional school setting. At home, students have the opportunity to set personal goals and work toward them without the added stress of others’ opinions.

For instance, consider a student who is studying alone and encounters difficulties during an online class. Instead of feeling embarrassed asking for help publicly, the student might choose to research the problem independently, thus building self-reliance and critical thinking skills. Additionally, if the student has a busy day filled with other activities, studying at home allows for flexibility. They can quickly take a break to prepare a meal or recharge, and then return to their studies without the need for rigid scheduling. If clarification is needed, the student can simply text a teacher without the pressure of speaking face-to-face.

The flexibility of an online learning environment is particularly helpful for those who are shy or require individualized attention. Some students might struggle with the early morning schedule at school, but studying at home gives them the option to work later in the day or even at night when they feel more alert. Consider also the case of pregnant students who face unique challenges. I have heard from friends about how difficult it was for a pregnant classmate to cope with the demands of attending school physically. Managing her condition alongside her studies became much less stressful when she shifted to online classes, as she could study from home while meeting her personal needs. This example reinforces the idea that learning from home can be less taxing for students in special circumstances.

There are, however, some challenges to consider with online learning. Not every student has the financial resources to access online classes or the proper equipment, and balancing both work and study can be difficult. Nevertheless, for those juggling jobs and education, the flexibility of remote learning might actually be beneficial. For instance, students can work for a few hours, then return home to complete assignments at their own pace, or alternate days between working and studying. This approach can help ensure that students do not miss many days of coursework and remain committed to their studies.

Online learning also offers several practical benefits. It encourages spending time on the computer for research, enables students to concentrate on homework with fewer interruptions, and allows easy access to information using mobile devices. Being at home can help reduce distractions from friends or uncomfortable social interactions that sometimes occur in school hallways. Additionally, studying from home removes concerns like dealing with cold weather or choosing the right outfit, all of which contribute to a more relaxed learning atmosphere.

In conclusion, the option to attend classes remotely has the potential to make learning a more comfortable and productive experience for many students. Although challenges such as financial limitations exist, the benefits—including flexibility, reduced social pressures, and the ability to manage individual needs—suggest that home-based learning is a valuable alternative for those who might struggle in a conventional classroom environment. With determination and the willingness to seek help when necessary, every student can succeed, no matter where they choose to study.

Changing the cafeteria menu is not a wise decision because many students might not like the food, some could suffer allergic reactions, and the waste of food could result in financial loss for the school. Many students are very particular about what they eat and may reject meals that do not meet their expectations. If the food seems unappealing or smells odd, most students will simply avoid it or discard it, leaving them hungry until they can eat elsewhere.

At this stage, students tend to be very choosy about their meals. They inspect their food to ensure it looks and smells acceptable. Personally, I am also very selective, and if I am going to eat something, I want it to look professionally prepared. This level of pickiness means that even a slight change to the menu might lead to most students refusing to eat the provided food.

It is also important to consider that some students suffer from allergies. Although having a food allergy might seem unusual to others, it is a normal and serious medical condition. Many kids feel embarrassed or scared to talk about their allergies for fear of being teased by their peers. Without proper and accurate information about these allergies, adjusting the menu could endanger these students.

Several schools invest a lot of money in updating their lunch programs to please students, but with so many picky eaters, the new meals might end up mostly untouched and discarded. This situation is detrimental, causing schools to waste money on food that the students do not appreciate. Instead of risking student satisfaction and financial loss, it is better to maintain the current menu, ensuring that students get meals they know they will eat while also protecting those with allergies.

I agree with Emerson’s idea, as holding a master's qualification helps individuals work more effectively, opens up better opportunities, and leads to higher positions than for those without it.

Some people, however, argue that success isn’t solely dependent on having a master's degree. They believe that sometimes individuals without this credential may outperform those who possess it.

To begin with, earning a master's qualification means you have spent years studying and practicing, which allows you to perform your job more efficiently. For example, in a restaurant, a chef with advanced training might only need to memorize the main recipes, while others must also remember various condiments, tools, and equipment.

In addition, having a master's degree often paves the way for expanded career opportunities. It serves as a formal proof of your preparation and skills, making you a more attractive candidate for certain roles. Many companies require a master's degree for key positions, much like some restaurants need a master-trained professional to take on management roles, which typically come with higher compensation.

Finally, a master's qualification can help you secure better positions. It demonstrates your experience and knowledge to employers. For instance, in a restaurant setting, the individual with a master's is more likely to be considered for a managerial role, while someone without it might start in a lower position, such as a dishwasher, and would need considerable effort and time to move up.

In conclusion, those with a master's qualification tend to have improved job performance, access to better opportunities, and a greater chance of securing higher positions. For these reasons, I support Emerson's view that without a master's, significant career growth may be hindered.

Have you ever come across something on the ground, picked it up, and pretended it belonged to you? This kind of behavior is dishonest and can lead to real problems. When you take something without trying to find its owner, you may be depriving someone of something they worked hard to own. As a child, I noticed many instances where people accidentally dropped their belongings. I made it a habit to return lost items or alert the person who dropped them. Unfortunately, not everyone follows this example, and many simply grab what they find. Without knowing the true owner, taking an item is essentially stealing.

Many people suggest leaving lost items where they lie because the rightful owner will likely return looking for them. After all, no one leaves something of value behind and then walks away without concern. I remember my elementary school having posters reminding us to leave what we found alone. Although several students listened to these messages, some still acted on impulse without considering the consequences. There's a great difference between needing something, which might be essential for daily life, and merely wanting something as a treat or even to show off. If you really need something important, you can always purchase it, but taking something that doesn't belong to you is wrong, regardless of your reasons.

If you find something on the ground, don't make it yours. Instead, if you see someone drop an item, make an effort to return it or let them know. Think about your actions before you act on peer pressure or selfish impulses. Being kind and helpful are qualities that can prevent misunderstandings and hurt feelings.

Consider the frustration someone feels when they lose something valuable, like a favorite toy or an expensive phone. Imagine how upset you would be if you dropped your cherished item and someone picked it up without any concern for returning it. On the other hand, if a stranger returned your lost item without expecting anything in return, you would feel grateful and relieved. I once lost my iPad because someone took it without thinking about its owner. Although I didn't know who took it, I was heartbroken and had to rely on my mother's phone until my dad could replace it. This experience taught me that taking something that isn't yours can have serious consequences.

Many items, especially expensive ones like smartphones, hold great value to their owners. When these items are lost or stolen, the owner can be devastated, as replacing them is no simple feat. People today depend on their phones for communication, safety, and staying connected, so losing one can create a significant problem. If someone were to steal my phone, I would be extremely upset and angry. It is important to remember that respecting others' property by returning lost items is a sign of honesty and integrity.

Have you ever wondered why some students finish their studies at a younger age? Some people argue that graduating early isn’t a good idea, but I believe that completing school early helps young people become more mature and responsible in the real world.

One main reason that early graduation is beneficial is that it prepares students for the realities of life. Many teenagers today have little understanding of how the world actually works. For example, some young people might engage in risky behaviors like drinking and driving without fully grasping the consequences until it is too late. Often, their parents step in to resolve the issues, which may prevent them from learning important lessons about accountability. By graduating early, teenagers are more likely to face real-life challenges firsthand, learning from their mistakes without relying on parental intervention.

In addition, early graduation encourages financial responsibility. When young individuals start paying for their own bills—such as rent, utility expenses, or even mobile phone bills—they begin to understand the value of money and the consequences of poor financial decisions. For instance, if a teenager is required to cover a portion of their monthly bills, they are more likely to monitor their usage and avoid unnecessary expenses. This hands-on experience with budgeting and financial planning is a crucial step in transitioning from adolescence to adulthood.

Some may claim that finishing school too early might cause one to miss out on valuable experiences or lead to stress, but I believe that the benefits of developing independence and responsibility far outweigh these concerns. Early graduation allows young people to learn how to navigate the complexities of life, understanding not only what actions are right but also what consequences might follow from poor choices.

In conclusion, graduating early is a positive step because it helps teenagers mature and become fully responsible for their own actions. It prepares them for the challenges of the real world and teaches them how to manage both their personal finances and their behavior, setting a strong foundation for their future.

Students should be allowed the freedom to opt for electives that truly interest them. When students engage in courses that make them happy and align with their natural talents, they are more likely to discover what they want to pursue in the future. Electives not only help uncover individual skills but also provide valuable opportunities down the road.

It is crucial that students have the power to choose the classes they enjoy. If they are forced into taking subjects they do not care about, it may lead to disinterest and skipping classes. This lack of engagement can result in poor grades, which may discourage them further, eventually affecting their high school graduation and college admission prospects. Without a solid academic record, finding a good job becomes even more challenging, leading to potential long-term consequences like unemployment and financial instability.

Every person has a unique talent, and exploring various electives enables students to nurture these strengths. When they excel in a subject they are passionate about, attending classes becomes a pleasure rather than a chore. Achieving high marks can increase their knowledge and confidence, opening doors to abundant opportunities in the professional world. For instance, a student with a flair for drama might eventually find success in acting, potentially earning significant recognition and income. Moreover, developing multiple skills can be extremely beneficial, as a well-rounded educational background often leads to greater professional success in the future.

Ultimately, the choices students make in school help shape their future. By pursuing electives that resonate with their interests and abilities, they set themselves on a path toward a smoother transition after high school and into college. Although life comes with its set of challenges, having a clear sense of direction and a portfolio of skills makes overcoming obstacles easier. Even if some critics argue that students might not take these classes seriously, the benefits of identifying and honing one's talents far outweigh the potential risks.

Therefore, dealing with these situations outside regular school time will decrease the number of class periods missed by students.

Furthermore, we must not forget the teachers who are also parents and need an extra day for family time and for carrying out regular activities with their children if they have them.

Likewise, consider the situation of seniors, who are facing one of the most difficult periods in their lives while deciding about their future. They need time to keep all options open for universities and colleges for the next step in higher education, as well as to consider jobs on weekends. Similarly, freshmen—children transitioning from middle school—also need understanding as they adjust to extra activities in high school that differ from their previous routines.

In addition, an option for a free day on Friday or Monday can be used for community service, with parental permission and some adult supervision. In this case, any student who wishes to participate can help by cleaning up streets and rivers or by contributing in any other community service ways. Moreover, the schools can create programs that involve big companies willing to help students find a job on this new free day, which may even serve as part-time work on weekends.

Nevertheless, always remember that being involved in two different activities per day can be hard and exhausting. In other words, going to school and then going to work is exhausting because you do not have enough time to rest. On the other hand, if you have only four school days—even though the school day is increased by two hours—you will have time after school for rest, to complete any project or homework, and to use the other three days for any job you think is convenient.

The idea of a four-day school week is one that should be considered not only by businesses but also by high schools and universities. This proposal suggests reducing the school week by one day, while compensating for the lost hours by extending each of the remaining days.

By eliminating one day, students would lose approximately ten hours of class time each week. However, this time could be replaced by lengthening the school day by two hours, which would allow for deeper focus on class subjects and more thorough completion of assignments and projects. These extra hours could also be used for additional support if a student is struggling with a subject, as there would be more time for interaction between teachers and students.

One possible use of the additional hours on the shortened week is to offer extended periods in the library. Such time could greatly benefit students who enjoy reading, as well as those who wish to participate in sports or other activities after school. The extra day off, which would replace the regular school day, could also serve as a convenient option for scheduling medical appointments or tending to health issues. Often, students miss classes due to necessary absences verified by a parent's note; having the day off regularly would lessen these disruptions.

Additionally, teachers who are also parents might appreciate having more time for family activities, which could help them balance responsibilities at home and work. This new schedule could be particularly beneficial for seniors who face important decisions about future education and careers. It might also assist younger students transitioning from middle school into high school, easing their adjustment process.

Another advantage of having a free day, whether on Friday or Monday, is that it can be used for community service with parental permission and adult supervision. Students could participate in local projects, such as street or river clean-ups, or even join programs organized by schools in partnership with businesses to explore part-time job opportunities.

On the other hand, one concern is that students with part-time jobs might find that a longer school day reduces their available work hours. However, students could potentially use the extra free day for full-time employment, balancing both school and work responsibilities.

In conclusion, while there are challenges to consider—such as the potential for exhaustion from a longer school day—the benefits seem to outweigh the disadvantages for most students. With more time for study, rest, family, and work, a move toward a four-day school week appears to be a positive change. If we all come together in support of this idea, we can advocate for a new right for high school and college students to enjoy more free time and a more flexible schedule.

People should trust their own thoughts and follow their instincts because personal confidence is the foundation of success. When you rely primarily on your internal judgment rather than on the opinions of others, you are more likely to develop unique ideas that reflect who you are.

To begin with, relying on your own judgment means believing in yourself. Rather than spending time worrying about what others think, you are able to generate creative ideas that come directly from your mind. This personal approach allows for independence in decision-making, whether the task is brainstorming new concepts or writing an original piece. It means that you do not need to constantly seek external validation or imitate someone else’s work.

Furthermore, following your instincts prepares you to handle difficult situations on your own. When challenges arise, trusting yourself means you are more likely to take immediate action instead of waiting for someone else to intervene. This self-reliance builds a stronger sense of confidence, which in turn enables you to navigate problems without needing excessive guidance. Being confident in your abilities means you are better equipped to make decisions that are swift and authentic.

Additionally, self-belief plays a crucial role in persuading others to trust you as well. For example, when you are required to present in front of a group but doubt your capabilities, this lack of conviction might be sensed by your audience, including your teacher. In such instances, the teacher’s confidence in you may waver, potentially affecting your performance grade. Conversely, if you show that you believe in your ideas and abilities, others are more likely to take you seriously and support your efforts.

In conclusion, it is important for individuals to trust their own instincts and ideas because self-belief is essential for personal growth and independent decision-making. Relying on oneself not only fosters originality, but it also builds the confidence needed to overcome challenges and gain the respect of others. Ultimately, by valuing your own thoughts, you create a strong foundation that encourages both personal success and the ability to inspire trust in those around you.

I have a natural talent for drawing, and I really enjoy creating images of stars, the moon, forests, and oceans. My favorite art is drawing because it allows me to create anything I imagine, and if I make a mistake, I can always correct it. I also love painting, as it lets me portray my emotions—whether I am feeling sad, happy, angry, or upset.

Art is a special talent that offers unlimited creative freedom and has the power to generate significant value. People are willing to spend a lot of money on unique pieces, sometimes even billions, simply because they see beauty in it. Many talented individuals create art, but sometimes they doubt its worth and discard their work. What they might not realize is that someone else could appreciate it and be eager to purchase it. While some artists choose to keep their art as a keepsake or pass it on to family, others decide to sell their creations, believing that their work deserves recognition and financial reward.

I believe that artists should consider selling their art, as it can bring in a good income while also sharing their creativity with the world. Art demands patience because there are moments when things do not go as planned, forcing you to start over. However, these mistakes can lead to unexpected beauty, transforming something initially flawed into a stunning piece.

Some people might think art is dull, but for those who love it, it is anything but. When you enjoy creating art, every moment spent painting fills you with joy and excitement. Sometimes, I even lose complete control over my hand, allowing my emotions to guide the brush and leading to surprising outcomes. It is that natural flow of creativity that makes the whole process so gratifying.

Although I sometimes feel stressed when my drawing does not meet my expectations, I remind myself that art is not an easy task—it requires perseverance and practice. Even though I am confident in my abilities, I understand that continuous practice is the key to mastering my craft. With time and patience, even the challenges in art become more manageable, and each mistake is simply another opportunity to learn and improve.

Students do not truly gain anything from attending classes from home. In my experience, a friend who took advantage of this option ended up neglecting her studies, using the extra freedom to prioritize other activities. Instead of enhancing her education, she misused the opportunity, proving that remote learning might actually harm students' academic progress.

To begin with, many students use the flexibility of home-based learning to focus on tasks that do not relate to their education. Some take advantage by turning in assignments late or avoiding deadlines altogether. Although not every student behaves this way, those who do often choose to indulge in distractions rather than concentrating on their work. They frequently use the extra time to engage in social outings, spend time with loved ones, or simply indulge in leisure activities instead of fulfilling their academic responsibilities.

Furthermore, this arrangement often leads to a lack of accountability. When given assignments or projects, some students opt for laziness because there is no immediate supervision. Without the direct presence of a teacher, students may feel less pressure to complete their work timely, spending hours on non-academic pursuits instead of studying. Even though many understand the material, they choose not to apply themselves seriously, missing out on knowledge that would benefit them in the long run.

Ultimately, the home-based learning environment can result in little to no real education. With the distractions of parties, social gatherings, and other personal commitments, students might resort to copying others' work or finding quick answers online instead of engaging with the subject matter. This approach to learning turns what should be a serious educational experience into a chance to slack off and put fun before academic improvement.

In summary, allowing students to attend classes from home does not serve their best interests. They often misuse the privilege by neglecting their responsibilities, missing out on essential learning, and focusing on personal enjoyment rather than their studies.

In contrast, many students benefit from the comfort of learning at home. Research has shown that students often prefer remote classes because they can arrange their seating and study environment to suit their personal needs, something that a traditional classroom setting typically does not allow. I share this view since having options for one’s seating arrangement can lead to a more pleasant learning experience.

Moreover, the issue of safety cannot be ignored. Recent incidents, such as numerous school shootings and the influence of negative peer groups, underscore the dangers present in some school environments. Learning from home reduces exposure to these risks, providing a secure alternative that eases parental concerns about their child’s well-being.

Overall, while critics emphasize the potential loss of group interaction, the benefits of enhanced comfort and safety make attending classes at home a viable and advantageous option.

Some schools have established programs that bring together older and younger students, and these initiatives offer benefits to both groups. These programs allow older students to learn more about responsibility, while younger students get a glimpse of what to expect as they grow up. At the same time, the older students benefit from fresh insights and different approaches that the younger ones share.

Older students are in a good position to share the lessons they have learned from their own mistakes. Since everyone makes errors, these students can provide guidance on how to avoid common pitfalls, offering advice that helps the younger ones make better choices. In this way, both groups learn – older students reinforce their own understanding and younger students receive valuable life lessons.

Meanwhile, younger students are able to see their mistakes reflected in the experiences of their older peers. Having older students available to listen to their problems or answer questions can be very reassuring. For example, when a young student struggles with learning English or faces other challenges, a more experienced student can offer support and practical guidance. In addition, older students sometimes rely on younger peers to gain a fresh perspective on matters they might not fully understand.

Both age groups benefit when they work together. Younger students often need advice much like they would get from an adult, just as older students sometimes need a reminder about proper conduct or perspective. For instance, if a conflict arises among younger students, an older student can help resolve the issue by encouraging them to make better decisions. Although younger students have a smaller set of responsibilities compared to older students, the mutual support between the two groups can create a more harmonious educational environment.

I remember that my father once shared how he hesitated to seek help when he was young. His experience taught me the importance of accepting guidance from someone with more experience, as it can save a lot of trouble down the road. In a similar way, older students can play a crucial role in helping younger ones understand the difference between right and wrong, fostering a safe atmosphere where mistakes are corrected before they become bigger problems.

Despite these benefits, challenges can occur when older students are not willing to support their younger peers, or when younger students refuse advice. This breakdown in communication might duplicate issues later on, as both groups might begin dismissing helpful guidance from teachers and adults. It is important for older students to remain engaged and for everyone to appreciate that respectful advice is meant to protect and help them. Ultimately, the exchange between older and younger students is essential for building a community where everyone learns from one another and grows together.

In my view, the journey toward achieving a goal or dream might involve many setbacks, but giving up is never an option. Thus, I disagree with the idea that constant failure is essential for achieving success. Life always offers another chance, and it is important to keep pushing forward. Although failure can be discouraging, it is possible to recover and try a different approach if one plan does not work. There is always more than one route to success, and sometimes exploring new possibilities can lead to unexpected rewards.

Maintaining enthusiasm is equally important. Your passion for something should drive you forward—you must take ownership of that zeal and not allow others to dampen it. Not everyone experiences strong feelings of inspiration, which makes it even more valuable when it appears. I learned this firsthand when I moved to the United States as a child; despite initially struggling with the language, my determination and enthusiasm eventually helped me excel in English.

In conclusion, success does not simply come from a series of failures. While setbacks are inevitable, they can be overcome with hard work and an unwavering commitment to your dreams. Never lose the passion that fuels your ambition, and continue striving, even when times seem tough.

One skill I have is reading aloud, and it really improves my understanding of the text. When I read aloud, the information sticks in my mind better, which makes it easier to explain what I’ve read. This also benefits me when I need to write an essay about the material.

Reading out loud helps me grasp the content more clearly and even allows me to monitor my own reading. I can tell if I am reading smoothly or if I tend to pause too much, and then I know when I should slow down to understand difficult words better.

This method not only boosts my comprehension but also enhances my ability to describe the story in detail. By vocalizing the words, I pick up on finer details that I might miss when reading silently. This practice helps me retain the information, as I often forget parts of the text if I don’t read it out loud. In addition, I find that others may also benefit from reading aloud to fully engage with the material.

When it comes to writing essays, reading aloud is particularly useful. It lets me gather many details about what I’ve read, and I feel more confident in my work because the content stays fresh in my memory. As a result, when I sit down to write, I already have a thorough understanding of the book, ensuring my essay accurately reflects the original message.

In short, reading aloud is a key technique for me. It strengthens my comprehension, aids in essay writing, and helps the information remain vivid in my mind.

Technology has significantly changed the way we live and interact, and I believe its impact is not entirely positive. Many argue that technology distances family members and prevents them from spending quality time together. This perspective highlights the fact that excessive use of modern devices can interfere with human connections. Key issues include phone addiction, compulsive online shopping, and a decline in personal communication.

For example, many individuals become overly attached to their smartphones or computer games, focusing exclusively on virtual entertainment. This obsession can lead them to ignore important real-life responsibilities, such as helping someone in need. Whether young or old, a person absorbed in their digital world may prioritize their device or game over providing support to others, which undermines the sense of community and empathy.

Similarly, while online shopping offers convenience, it can also become an addictive behavior. Some people find themselves repeatedly buying items online, which may initially signify independence but can eventually lead to a pattern of excessive spending. This habit not only affects personal finances but also detracts from genuine social interactions and experiences.

Additionally, when people lose the habit of engaging in face-to-face communication, they often miss out on motivational opportunities that help shape their future and personal growth. Without meaningful interactions, individuals might struggle to find inspiration and direction in life.

In conclusion, although technology brings many advantages, its negative effects on personal relationships and social behavior cannot be ignored. Too much reliance on devices and online activities may isolate individuals and hinder their ability to connect with the people around them. This is why I believe that technology, despite its benefits, is not the greatest creation of humanity.
