Albert Einstein once said that "imagination is more important than knowledge," and I completely agree with his view. Imagination not only brings personal joy but also has the power to help others and even lead you to a fulfilling career. This essay will explore these ideas.

To begin with, using your imagination can brighten your own life. When you let your mind wander to things you enjoy, you feel happier. For instance, even if you cannot actually fly like a bird, you can imagine what it would be like—feeling the freedom or the thrill of the experience—and this mental escape can be very uplifting. Similarly, picturing what your life might be like in the future, such as imagining yourself at 100 years old, can bring comfort and satisfaction.

Furthermore, imagination can be a great tool in helping others. Consider a situation where a young child is upset in a shopping center, perhaps because of the way she is dressed and the attention it attracts from others. By encouraging her to see her outfit in a different light, such as comparing her look to that of a princess visiting someone special, you might help her calm down. This imaginative approach not only soothes her feelings but also turns the situation into a positive moment.

Finally, many believe that relying solely on imagination will not secure the desired career, but I disagree. Imagine someone aiming to become a successful home designer without the creative spark—his designs might fail, leading to a loss of income. On the other hand, a writer with a vivid imagination might produce many outstanding books, achieving financial success that rivals even high-paying professions like doctors. Thus, a strong imagination can be the key to finding a rewarding job.

In conclusion, I firmly support Einstein's claim that imagination holds greater importance than knowledge. It enriches our lives, helps us assist others in tough moments, and even opens doors to careers that bring personal and financial satisfaction. For me, imagination is indeed one of the most valuable qualities anyone can possess.

Working in groups offers many important benefits, especially for students. When everyone collaborates, people can support one another, share ideas, and create better work together. Group work encourages students to learn new skills and build relationships, which not only helps them succeed in their studies but also prepares them for future careers and personal life. In my view, teachers should encourage group work because it promotes better understanding, fosters communication, and creates an environment where everyone can contribute their strengths.

One major advantage of working in groups is the variety of ideas that can emerge when several people share their thoughts. When a student feels lost or unsure about a task, the help of a group member can make a big difference. This collaborative effort often leads to higher quality work as students discuss, clarify, and build on each other’s ideas. In addition, working in groups helps students improve their communication skills. Expressing thoughts clearly and understanding others is key, not only in academic work but also in everyday life situations such as in the workplace or at home.

Another benefit is the opportunity to learn essential skills through teamwork. By interacting with classmates, students can develop their ability to write, speak, and solve problems together. Those who grasp a concept quickly can assist others, making the learning process smoother for everyone involved. This type of cooperation is particularly useful when language barriers or misunderstandings occur, as students can support each other in overcoming these challenges.

Group work also provides a valuable social experience. Working closely with peers helps students make new friends and build a network of support within the classroom. These social connections can lead to a more positive and engaging learning environment. Moreover, the ability to work well with others is a skill that will benefit individuals far beyond their school years. In many professional settings, teamwork is essential, and those who are comfortable collaborating with others are more likely to succeed.

While working alone might sometimes allow for better concentration, the benefits of group work can outweigh this drawback. When a student struggles on their own, the collective knowledge of a group can offer a fresh perspective and much-needed assistance. Therefore, increasing group assignments could lead to improved overall performance and better preparation for future challenges.

In conclusion, group work is a valuable method for students to learn and grow. By sharing ideas and relying on each other’s strengths, students can complete tasks more effectively while also prepping themselves for the social and collaborative demands of the workplace and life. It is clear that fostering environments where students work in groups can have a lasting, positive impact on their academic success and future endeavors.

Collaborating within a group offers numerous advantages that significantly ease and speed up the process of completing an assignment. When working with others, tasks are divided, and everyone contributes their own ideas and perspectives, which ultimately leads to a more efficient and effective solution. In contrast, working by yourself means shouldering all the responsibilities and often spending more time on the same task.

With multiple people involved, the work is typically finished more quickly than if one were to tackle it alone.

This person ensures that everyone is accountable and that tasks are assigned fairly, which minimizes disagreements over responsibilities. Without group support, a single person facing such challenges would have no backup.

You might not be able to resolve the issue at hand, and if you try your best and it doesn't work out, you may make the problem even worse.

There's a problem with your sink and you don't know how to fix it. So, what do you do? You call a plumber to repair your sink pipes. The plumber goes away to do another job, and your sink starts to leak again. You try to fix it because you were watching the plumber do it the first time, but the water leak gets worse and floods your house. Now you have to call the plumber again and pay again, when you could have called him before it started leaking again so he could have walked you through it.

Some kids have pets, and when those pets pass away, their parents sometimes try to replace the pet with another. This can be hard for the child, who might not eat, sleep, or even talk for a long time. When my dog Lucky died, it was hard for my brother and me; we barely ate or talked, and our dad tried to get another dog, but we both knew it wasn't going to be the same.

When you're in school and you notice a sad kid and ask him, "What's wrong?" and he doesn't say anything back, you start talking about coming over after school because you have to do a project with him. You say, "Ask your dad if I can come over." Then the kid starts to cry because his dad passed away in a car accident last night, and he tells you the news. You made him feel worse than he did 20 minutes ago just by saying one simple thing.

So, American jazz legend Duke Ellington, I disagree with your statement, because you can make many things worse than they originally were by trying to fix them—whether it's trying to fix a sink, replace a pet that has passed away, or make someone feel happy when your attempt only ends up worsening their feelings.

Duke Ellington once claimed that "A problem is a chance for you to do your best." This statement suggests that difficulties provide an opportunity to improve and solve them before they worsen. However, I disagree with Ellington’s idea. There are times when trying to address a problem only makes matters more complicated, as not every issue has a clear or workable solution.

Consider a situation where your sink is malfunctioning and you clearly cannot repair it yourself. The logical solution might be to call a plumber. But if the plumber finishes the repair and then leaves, only for the sink to start dripping again, your attempt to fix the problem may inadvertently lead to a bigger issue—such as flooding your home. This means you might have to summon the plumber once again, incurring extra costs and stress, even though a timely professional intervention could have prevented the escalation.

Another example involves the loss of a pet. When a beloved animal dies, replacing it with another may not bring comfort to a grieving child. Instead, the replacement might remind the child of what they lost, leading to a deeper sense of sadness. I experienced this myself when our family dog, Lucky, passed away. Neither my brother nor I could easily start over, and even though my father tried to bring home a new dog, we all sensed that nothing could fill the void left by Lucky.

Finally, imagine trying to comfort a classmate who is visibly upset. A seemingly innocent invitation to come over after school might unintentionally worsen his sorrow, especially if he has just lost someone close. In these scenarios, the effort to mend a situation sometimes amplifies the original problem.

Therefore, while Ellington’s perspective may work in some cases, it is clear that attempting to solve every issue can sometimes lead to unintended and more serious consequences.

Working in a group offers more advantages compared to working alone. When you are part of a team, you can gather ideas, share information, and receive support while completing projects. Collaborating allows you to exchange thoughts and ask questions, which helps everyone improve their work through discussion and shared examples.

There are many positive aspects of working together. For instance, you have the opportunity to discuss your assignments with others, ask for clarification, and benefit from different approaches and solutions that teammates suggest. This type of collaboration not only improves the quality of the work but also makes it easier to generate ideas because you are not solely responsible for every detail.

On the other hand, working by yourself has fewer advantages. While it offers the freedom to develop your own ideas without interruption, you lose the support that comes from collaborating with peers. You might need to spend extra time gathering information and verifying that your work is accurate, as there is no one else to review your ideas or provide feedback.

For example, during high school, an English teacher might assign a project where students work in groups of four. In such a setting, one student could gather the necessary information, another might focus on writing, a third might collect examples, and the last could read the final project and present it in class. This division of tasks not only reduces individual stress but also improves the overall quality of the project through mutual support.

In contrast, if a student chooses to work alone on the same project, they might appreciate having uninterrupted time to think. However, this approach makes it more challenging to gather diverse perspectives and ensure that all aspects of the project are covered. Working alone can lead to feelings of isolation, and without discussion, some ideas may not be fully explored.

Ultimately, while some people may prefer to work independently because they find it less distracting or feel more comfortable working in silence, most choose group work because it allows them to connect with friends, exchange ideas, and enhance the quality of their work through teamwork.

One activity I consider really enjoyable is science experiments. One reason I find these activities fun is that they are different from other types of projects; for example, while a math or language arts project merely involves doing many exercises or writing an essay, science projects offer something different. For instance, one time I got to see a frog's interior. It might sound disgusting to many readers, and to be honest, it did not smell good either. Yet one thing that fascinated me about the project was that frogs do not have as many organs as we humans do, or maybe some had been removed, but there were not many organs present.

Another thing I was curious about was that the frog's insides were different colors; I remember seeing blue and pink, unlike us humans, whose insides are almost entirely red. The frog's interior had different colors, although it looked a little dry because my teacher told me that the frog had been frozen for some time. However, this state definitely made it easier to cut parts from the frog’s interior. Since my teacher said we were able to cut whatever we wanted, my group and I tried to explore as much as possible. There was one part that was really disgusting: there were some flies in the frog's stomach, and that definitely disgusted me, though it did not make me want to stop.

After we finished examining everything inside the frog, the teacher explained the name and function of each part. However, one of my friends decided it was silly to poke the frog's eye, and I still do not know what went through his mind at that moment. When he poked it, the frog's eye—not completely frozen—released liquid that came rushing out and soaked him. Fortunately, it did not reach me, but it definitely reached my mate, and after that the teacher sent him to the bathroom to wash himself.

After that, my teacher decided it was best to stop the project, but it was definitely a lot of fun.

Another example of a project occurred recently when my teacher decided to have us do a project in the dark, which was themed to what we are learning about—the unit of light. The project was very simple and, to be honest, it wasn't as amazing or funny as the other project; we were just supposed to spray a liquid in front of a flashlight so that we could see the waves on which light travels. After the teacher explained the process, she told us to spray the liquid in front of the flashlight. Honestly, I didn't see anything at first and was kind of disappointed, but after four seconds I could see the waves, although they were hard to see and lasted only a few seconds. Still, I actually enjoyed the project, despite some downsides such as its short duration and the teacher taking forever to explain the process. Overall, I still think it was a really interesting project.

In sharing these examples from my own personal experiences, I tried to show that science experiments are not always boring. You might not like them at first, but you should give them a chance because I promise that you are going to like them—or at least one of the many projects available. They make class a little more interesting, and in my opinion, projects or experiments are the best activities in school because they offer a more direct type of learning. That's why I think they are the best.

I find science experiments to be among the most enjoyable school activities. The reason behind this is that these experiments differ greatly from other assignments. For instance, while math or language projects typically involve repetitive exercises or writing essays, science experiments present entirely unique experiences. I remember one experiment in which I got the chance to observe the inside of a frog. Although it might sound unappealing—and admittedly, it wasn’t a pleasantly scented experience—it captured my attention because it revealed that frogs have far fewer organs than humans. It was intriguing to see how nature designs different creatures, with perhaps some organs having been removed or simply not present.

Another fascinating aspect of the experiment was discovering that the internal parts came in various colors. I recall noticing shades of blue and pink, unlike humans, whose insides are predominantly red. The colors were somewhat altered by the freezing process the frog had undergone, which also made it easier to dissect, allowing my group and me to explore as much as we could. Yet, there was a moment that I found particularly gross when we encountered some flies in the frog’s stomach. Despite this unsettling detail, my curiosity remained undeterred.

After our hands-on exploration, our teacher explained the function and name of each part of the frog. However, one of my classmates thought it was amusing to poke the frog’s eye. I still wonder what he was thinking at that moment. When he poked it, the part of the eye that had not fully frozen started to leak liquid, getting him soaked. Fortunately, I was not affected, though it did hit one of my friends, who was then sent to wash up in the bathroom. Because of that incident, our teacher decided to stop the dissection.

In another experiment, our teacher organized a project in a dark room in line with our current unit on light. The project was simple, though not as memorable or amusing as the frog experiment. The task involved spraying a liquid in front of a flashlight to reveal the wave patterns of light. Initially, I didn’t see anything, which left me somewhat disappointed. However, after a few seconds, faint waves became visible, and although the phenomenon lasted only a short time, I enjoyed watching it. The experiment had its drawbacks, such as its brief duration and the lengthy explanation beforehand, but overall, it still proved to be an interesting activity.

Through sharing these experiences, I hope to show that science experiments can be far from dull. Even if you think you might not enjoy them, I encourage you to try and give them a chance. They add an extra level of excitement to class and, in my opinion, projects and experiments offer the best kind of learning—one that is direct and engaging.

While some schools permit cell phones for academic uses, misuse of these devices has become an ongoing issue. Instead of supporting their learning, many students use their phones to search for test answers or to message peers during class. Students who openly use their phones in class are likely to be caught quickly; however, others try to hide their devices so that teachers do not notice. Many even resort to sneaking peeks at their phones by checking their bags, pockets, or backpacks. Despite these attempts to conceal their actions, teachers often manage to identify the students involved. Whether the phones are used openly or in secret, the constant presence of these devices makes it difficult for students to focus on the lesson.

Additionally, some parents have received complaints from their child's school about inappropriate phone use. In these cases, parents are required to collect the device, which sometimes leads students to covertly retrieve their phone without permission to avoid further trouble. Even though parents warn against such behavior, the pattern of misuse seems likely to continue.

A small act of kindness can truly change someone's day. Even a brief gesture—a smile, a helping hand, or a kind word—holds the power to brighten someone’s mood and even improve their health. Many people may not receive that spark of joy daily, but a simple caring act can be exactly what they need, especially when they are facing personal struggles.

When someone experiences kindness, they often feel cherished and valued. It can bring warmth and happiness both inside and out, creating a strong sense of connection. This feeling of being loved is one of the most uplifting emotions, and it shows that you do not always need material gifts to make someone happy. A genuine act of care often means more than any physical present.

Furthermore, when you are on the receiving end of kindness, it frequently inspires you to pay it forward. Acts of kindness work like a chain reaction; when you help someone, you encourage them to help others in return. Whether it’s by offering assistance in everyday tasks or simply sharing a smile, these gestures strengthen our bonds and remind us of the importance of being there for one another.

Even within families, small acts of kindness play an essential role. They foster an environment where everyone feels appreciated and secure. Remember the saying by Aesop: "No act of kindness, no matter how small, is ever wasted." By passing on the kindness we receive, we contribute to a cycle of generosity and compassion that can transform lives, one kind act at a time.

It is often claimed that first impressions are nearly impossible to alter, and I completely agree with this idea for several reasons. When you first encounter someone, their behavior immediately influences your feelings toward them, whether you develop an attraction or a dislike. Furthermore, if you only meet that person once, the brief interaction may be the only basis on which you judge them, solidifying your opinion forever. Even if you encounter the same individual regularly, their initial behavior tends to shape your feelings and these impressions remain unchanged over time. Ultimately, this is why changing your first impression is such a difficult task.

The emotional response you experience, be it positive or negative, stems directly from how someone behaves during your initial meeting. For instance, I once met a person for the first time without any expectations. As our conversation unfolded, I found that I did not appreciate his way of speaking or his personality, and the negative impression I formed at that moment has stayed with me ever since. I have not met him again, and my opinion has never wavered. This clearly illustrates that once you form a view based on a first impression, it is very challenging to see things differently.

Even if you know nothing about it initially, the willingness to explore new techniques stems from a desire to challenge yourself and perhaps find a hidden talent. This curiosity motivates many people to try various activities, such as raising children, where every day presents new lessons in teaching right from wrong. Attempting these undertakings is not about guaranteed success but about discovering whether you can rise to the occasion.

Humans have an incredible capacity to overcome challenges by simply deciding to try. When you set your mind to a task, you might be surprised by your own resilience. History shows us how people have accomplished what once seemed impossible: gaining freedom from oppressive regimes, abolishing slavery, and fighting deeply ingrained racism. These milestones were reached because people were willing to face obstacles head-on, even when the tasks appeared daunting. In our own lives, each new challenge we face has the potential to bring out our inner strength, provided we do not give up when the going gets tough.

However, it is important to recognize that the fear of failure can sometimes cause us to hold back. When we experience repeated setbacks, our self-esteem may suffer, and we might begin to view ourselves as quitters. This internal criticism often brings more emotional pain than any physical hardship might, and it can hinder our progress even further. The emotional toll of such failures is significant; it can leave us feeling defeated and reluctant to take on new challenges. 

Some individuals, however, manage to navigate their emotions effectively. They understand the importance of confronting their feelings rather than suppressing them. Professionals like therapists work hard to master their own emotional responses in order to better support those who struggle with similar issues. Their success in managing emotional challenges is a reminder that personal growth often demands both the courage to try new things and the persistence to overcome internal obstacles.

Ultimately, our willingness to explore the unknown is fueled by curiosity and the hope of discovering something that truly resonates with us. Every new experience, whether it leads to immediate success or not, is an opportunity to learn more about what we are capable of achieving. As long as we continue to push our boundaries, we allow ourselves the chance to transform and improve. In this way, growth is not about avoiding risks or failures but about embracing the possibilities that come from trying new things, no matter the outcome.

Another benefit is that being at home allows teenagers to enjoy the safety and support of their families. Spending time with family members can provide a stable environment where they might do homework or engage in meaningful conversations about their future and the blessings they have.

Finally, adhering to such rules is important for maintaining order in the community. Failure to follow the curfew can lead to significant trouble, demonstrating the need for clear guidelines and the discipline to abide by them.

The prompt says "Unless you try something beyond what you have mastered, you will never grow." One would say that is something very wise to say. But due to the lack of wisdom around the world, it is basically useless to say anything wise. I personally agree, apart from physically growing, I'm almost done. Going back to the topic, I do agree with what author Ralph Waldo Emerson said in his quote: "That if you don't try something beyond what I have mastered, am I really growing in any way?"

Although I can't think of a reason why someone would disagree with the statement, I have tried many things in my seventeen years of being alive, and I can say I have grown to be the person I am now. Many people don't try new things, only because they are quick to judge the presentation of the new item or new person, but if people actually gave the new experience a chance, it could be life-changing for better or worse.

So, going back to you trying something beyond what I have mastered, I won't grow or something like that; it's all in perspective. If I wish to try something new and be a better person in society, I will, but if I wish to not try anything at all and just do the same boring routine day after day, sooner or later I will get bored of everything. Even though some may argue by saying, "That's how I got successful in the first place by doing the same routine over and over." In some cases, that may work; for example, in sports the athlete must do the same thing over and over until they get better at the sport, or, like in dance, they practice the same dance over and over until it's ready to be shared with the world, showing how well one can dance. And for others, trying a new routine can lead them to success (well, maybe not everyone is talented).

In conclusion, trying something new does change who you are in a bit by either helping or destroying you. People do grow to be wise and old, and others don't grow old wise—just young and reckless. Author Ralph Waldo Emerson was a wise man to say, "Unless you try something beyond what you already have mastered, you will never grow."

Even though some may argue, saying "that's how I got successful in the first place by doing the same routine over and over," in some cases that may work. For example, in sports the athlete must do the same thing repeatedly until they get better at the sport, or like a dancer, who practices the same dance over and over until it's ready to be shared with the world. And for others, trying a new routine can lead them to success (well, maybe not everyone is talented).

In conclusion, trying something new does change who you are, either by helping or destroying you. People do grow to be wise and old while others don't grow old wise, remaining just young and reckless. Author Ralph Waldo Emerson was a wise man to say, "Unless you try something beyond what you already have mastered you will never grow." Thank you for taking the time to read this essay.

"Unless you try something beyond what you have mastered, you will never grow." This statement holds a great deal of truth, yet its wisdom might seem insignificant if not put into practice. I firmly believe that while physical growth may have its limits, personal development is an ongoing process that requires stepping out of one’s comfort zone. Emerson's words resonate with me because sticking to what we already know does not allow us to truly evolve.

By continually following the same routine without exploring new opportunities, we limit our potential. In my own experience over my seventeen years of life, I have discovered that trying different things has helped shape who I am. Many individuals hesitate to embrace new experiences, often because they quickly judge what is unfamiliar. However, if people were willing to give new experiences a fair chance, they might find that these challenges can lead to significant personal transformation—whether for the better or sometimes even for the worse.

The idea that one cannot grow unless they venture beyond their mastered skills is all about perspective. If I want to improve and become a better person within society, I must be open to new challenges, even if that means breaking away from a monotonous routine. While some might claim that repeating the same actions is the key to success, as seen in sports or dance where athletes and performers perfect their craft through repetition, there is also great value in stepping out of that routine to discover untapped potential. Yet, it is important to acknowledge that individual paths to success vary, and not everyone will reach the same level of talent simply by following a new path.

In essence, trying something new can alter who you are in significant ways—it can build you up or, in some cases, lead to failure. Wisdom and maturity often come from taking risks and learning from them, while avoiding new experiences can leave one feeling stagnant and even reckless in youth. As Emerson wisely noted, unless you push past what you already know, real growth is impossible."

Failure plays an essential role in our path to success. Although failure may seem like a setback, it often serves as a stepping stone that leads us toward our goals. The idea behind Ralph Waldo Emerson's statement is that without experiencing failure, we may never learn how to handle and overcome life's challenges.

I support Emerson's perspective because encountering failure helps us become aware of our shortcomings. By going through setbacks, we develop resilience and gain an appreciation for the effort required to achieve real success.

However, there is another viewpoint that suggests relying too much on failure might hinder progress. Not knowing what to expect when things go awry could leave us unprepared for unforeseen circumstances. Although success brings its own rewards, some argue that encountering failure is necessary for growth because it underlines the unpredictable nature of life.

In conclusion, I believe that success and failure work together. While success is obviously desirable, failure provides important lessons that prepare us for unexpected challenges. Recognizing that setbacks are inevitable helps us develop the persistence needed to achieve our long-term goals.

However, when she helped someone, that student's project always turned out to be the best in the class because of her assistance.

Other people say that when they receive examples, they sometimes get confused. This happens when the examples change their perspective on what they are doing. For instance, when drawing, a teacher might instruct you to create an image based on your imagination—that is, your own thoughts. If the teacher then tells you what to draw after saying the drawing is about your imagination and provides examples, it makes you think that she wants you to draw something other than what you originally envisioned. This shows that sometimes examples do not work in specific subjects because they can cause confusion.

Although others say that using examples is more effective for influencing people because it demonstrates their experience and teaches how to do something, many people learn better and are more influenced by examples. I believe there are stronger methods that render examples less useful or even powerless in influencing others. For these reasons, I think there are better ways to influence people without using examples.

Have you ever found that you learn more effectively through varied approaches rather than just following examples? As Albert Schweitzer once noted, "Example is not the main thing to influence others." This suggests that there are alternative ways to have an impact on others without relying solely on examples.

One method of influence is to offer direct assistance instead of merely providing examples. For instance, in my ceramics class, the teacher usually demonstrated how to shape clay objects but rarely helped students individually. This approach made it challenging for both me and my classmates to grasp the process, as the instructions were given only once, and some students eventually forgot the details. On the other hand, when the teacher offered personal guidance, the outcomes were clearly superior, with those students producing the best work in the class.

Moreover, some people find that examples sometimes lead to confusion. This can occur when the examples shift their original perspective about what they are doing. Take drawing, for example: if a teacher first instructs students to create artwork from their imagination and then follows this with specific examples, it might lead the students to believe they are expected to follow those examples instead of their own ideas. This demonstrates that in certain situations, examples can be counterproductive and distract from the intended creative process.

Although there are arguments claiming that examples can be powerful, as they showcase expertise and offer a clear method to follow, I believe that direct support and guidance can provide stronger influence in many cases. For these reasons, I maintain that there are more effective ways to influence others without solely depending on examples.

Summer break is an essential time for students to relax and enjoy life after a lengthy period of academic work. During this vacation, families have the opportunity to travel, reconnect with loved ones, and engage in activities that provide a welcome distraction from the pressures of school. Students benefit from these months away from the classroom by reducing stress and having time to pursue personal interests that are difficult to explore during the busy school year. Whether it involves visiting new places, catching up with relatives, or simply enjoying leisure time, summer offers a much-needed escape.

In addition to recreation, the break provides practical benefits. For example, students who need to retake a class or recover lost credits can use this period to catch up on their studies. Similarly, those involved in sports often relish the extended time to practice and improve without academic interruptions. Avid readers also appreciate the long hours available to spend in libraries or at home with their favorite books. Moreover, students who enjoy traveling can document their experiences through journals or photographs, sharing stories and adventures with their peers once school resumes.

Reducing the summer vacation period would mean more time spent in the classroom and less opportunity for these valuable life experiences. It could lead to increased stress and limit the ability of students to explore interests outside of academic responsibilities. Thus, the idea of shortening summer breaks is not appealing, as it would take away the chance for students to relax, pursue hobbies, and maintain a balanced life.

I firmly support keeping the summer vacation intact. It offers a vital break from the intense school routine and allows students to rejuvenate, whether through travel, extracurricular activities, or simply enjoying quality time with family and friends. Maintaining a long summer break is crucial for fostering a healthy balance between education and personal well-being.

Over the past few years, students have been using cellphones more often than in the previous 15 years, when cellphones first became an essential part of daily life and were not allowed in the classroom. Times have changed, and now students are allowed to use their cellphones in the classroom. In this essay I want to answer the question, "What are the effects of allowing students to have and use cellphones in the classrooms?"

When cellphones were first allowed in the classroom, there were many benefits. It became easier for teachers and students to do their work, and for students it became easier to find information using their cellphones instead of a computer, especially when there were not enough computers for every student. Allowing students to use cellphones also helped teachers discover better ways to manage class work by using an app that might not be available on a computer. However, nothing is perfect; by allowing students to use their cellphones in the classroom, many began using them irresponsibly. For example, some students used their cellphones while the teacher was explaining a subject, and some used them to distract others during class.

These are some examples of the good and bad effects of allowing students to use their cellphones in the classroom.

Over recent years, students have become more reliant on cellphones, a stark contrast to the past 15 years when such devices were not seen as an essential part of daily life and were even banned in classrooms. Today, however, schools permit students to use their cellphones during lessons, opening the discussion on the impact of this change in policy.

Initially, the introduction of cellphones into the classroom brought several benefits. For one, both teachers and students found it easier to complete their work. Students could quickly search for information about various subjects, especially when there were not enough computers available for everyone. Teachers, on the other hand, discovered new and effective ways to conduct lessons by incorporating apps accessible only on mobile devices. Despite these advantages, there were downsides to this increased cellphone use in classrooms. Many students began to use their devices irresponsibly, such as checking their phones while the teacher was explaining important material or distracting their peers during class time.

This discussion highlights both the positive and negative consequences of allowing cellphones in the classroom.

I believe that curfews play an important role in safeguarding teenagers, especially during the late hours of the night. The primary aim of these restrictions is to protect young people from potential dangers, and in doing so, they ultimately benefit the very group they are designed to help.

Consider that the nighttime is often a period when supervision is limited, allowing teenagers the freedom to potentially engage in risky behavior. With a curfew in place, there is a clear expectation for adolescents to follow rules and avoid situations that could lead to trouble. Moreover, not only does a curfew prevent undesirable activity on the streets at night, but it also encourages everyone, including teenagers, to spend that time safely at home resting or enjoying family activities.

There is also a concern that the nighttime environment can expose individuals to criminal behavior, such as theft or other harm, particularly because fewer people are present to intervene. In this light, curfews serve as a preventive measure to protect not only property but also the well-being of those who might otherwise become involved in or witness dangerous events.

Some argue that nighttime activities, like visiting clubs, offer harmless fun. However, I maintain that such late-night excursions carry significant risks. There have been incidents, such as a tragic shooting in a club a few years ago, that highlight the potential dangers of being out late. Ultimately, curfews are a necessary step to ensure the safety and security of teenagers, and this protective approach proves beneficial for them in the long run.

Churchill once said that failure is essential in achieving success, and I believe his claim holds true, especially for those determined to improve their lives. Failure teaches us valuable lessons that help us grow. It also reveals who our true friends are, and it stresses the importance of not repeating the same mistakes.

Firstly, every failure carries its own lesson. As humans, we are bound to make errors throughout our lives. Those who pay attention to these lessons become more resilient and are better able to assist others facing similar challenges. Learning from our mistakes is crucial since life will always bring new obstacles.

Secondly, encountering failure often uncovers the genuine people in our lives. Sometimes, those we expected to be supportive might not be there when we stumble, while individuals we had underestimated might offer unexpected help. For example, a truly caring partner would stand by you even during tough times.

Lastly, it is important not to repeat the same mistake repeatedly. Constantly falling into the same trap can diminish our enthusiasm and make it harder to bounce back. Experiencing failure is inevitable, but if we do not learn from our errors, overcoming future challenges becomes much more difficult.

In conclusion, everyone faces failure at some point, but the real measure of success is the ability to move forward, having learned from those experiences. Change is possible for anyone willing to grow and learn from past mistakes.

A positive outlook is essential for achieving success and enjoying life. Maintaining a cheerful disposition not only enhances our own happiness but also uplifts the people around us. When you adopt a constructive mindset, you can face challenges with confidence and ease, regardless of what life throws at you.

For instance, consider a customer service worker who encounters negative feedback from a client. Even if the customer criticizes the work, the employee does not let this affect their spirits. They understand that the criticism is part of the job and remain confident in their abilities, continuing their work with a positive demeanor.

There are many advantages to keeping an optimistic attitude. When you notice that someone appears tired or upset, it is often a reflection of their surroundings or mindset. In contrast, displaying a friendly and energetic expression can inspire others and create a more welcoming environment. This readiness to engage positively can make everyday challenges seem less daunting and contribute to a more productive day.

Moreover, pursuing your goals with a positive attitude requires self-awareness and mutual respect. A confident and cheerful personality can convince others of your potential, whether you are aiming for a better job or planning significant projects. Your optimistic approach becomes a testament to your capability and readiness to take on new challenges.

During a job interview, for example, showing genuine enthusiasm and clearly outlining your skills can set you apart from other candidates. An honest and pleasant interaction not only demonstrates your competence but also reassures the interviewer that you are a good fit for the position.

Ultimately, it is widely recognized that a positive attitude is the driving force behind success. It opens doors to new opportunities, helps build meaningful relationships, and creates a foundation for a prosperous future. By carrying an optimistic outlook, you not only enrich your own life but also spread joy and inspiration to everyone you encounter.

Technology plays a vital role in our daily lives by enabling us to connect with others and complete various tasks at once. It allows individuals to communicate freely and make significant progress in their work. Personally, I have found that technology supports me in managing my routine responsibilities, simplifying many aspects of my daily schedule.

For instance, there are risks such as losing money through online banking issues. Despite these concerns, the benefits of technological advancements clearly outweigh the negative effects. The way we borrow books, shop online, or enjoy games has been completely transformed by technology. Furthermore, the availability of online tests highlights its potential to improve education and assessment methods.

In conclusion, while technology brings both advantages and disadvantages, its overall impact remains positive. With each passing day, our lives are increasingly improved by the tools and innovations of this century. Even though there are challenges related to reduced personal contact and financial risks, technology continues to enhance our efficiency and quality of life in numerous ways.

I agree with the statement because a first impression is incredibly hard to change, even when someone makes an effort to do so.

A first encounter leaves a lasting mark, affecting our attitude, emotions, and overall perception. Once these feelings are established, they tend to remain fixed and are difficult to modify. For instance, if someone is known for a particular style or behavior, it becomes challenging to present a completely different image, even if the intent is to impress or win someone's affection. When a person has been enchanted by someone since childhood, sudden changes in behavior won’t easily alter that initial perception.

Moreover, even if we try to replicate or adjust that initial impact, it seems nearly impossible because everyone recognizes the distinctiveness of a first impression. A good example might be when one individual uses a special recipe to charm another. Even if the second person attempts to recreate the same dish, the flavor will never quite match the original, as some secret ingredient or subtle touch is missing. This shows that the initial impression maintains its uniqueness and resists change.

It is clear that first impressions are deeply ingrained and can be as complex as emotional responses. Sometimes these early perceptions might even be based on misrepresentations. For example, a student might exaggerate details about their personality or background to gain acceptance among peers, and those early impressions may stick regardless of later revelations.

Ultimately, it is important to recognize that first impressions are remarkably resilient. Trying to alter someone’s initial perception or copying someone else’s approach is often futile, as the genuine nature of the first impression is something that remains with us, regardless of any subsequent efforts.

Although he might try to act as if nothing happened, the fact that everyone noticed makes it nearly impossible to remain unaffected. His face might turn red and feelings of embarrassment can overwhelm him, and these reactions are often beyond his control.

Typically, when an unusual or embarrassing first impression occurs only rarely, the feelings that follow—such as shame, confusion, or discomfort—can be particularly strong. However, if such moments happen frequently, they may eventually become part of everyday life and might even bring a sense of humor or happiness in hindsight. For instance, in my own life, even though my family sometimes asks awkward questions or we encounter embarrassing situations, these moments have become less intimidating over time.

Repeated experiences with first impressions can help individuals learn how to handle similar situations with greater ease. Over the years, I have experienced so many instances that what could once cause embarrassment now feels natural or even amusing. When my mother teases me about having a girlfriend, I find myself responding with a smile and a casual remark, and the initial shock quickly fades away. Similarly, when friends at school question me about my romantic interests, I answer normally without letting the situation embarrass me, as I have learned from past experiences.

Looking ahead, I hope that whenever I encounter a situation that might spark an embarrassing first impression, I can rely on my previous experiences to stay composed. This way, I can prevent the moment from escalating into something more overwhelming, ensuring that I remain calm and not let it disrupt my peace of mind.

Taking Classes Online Versus Attending School in Person

Some people argue that having classes online offers students extra time for their assignments and that working from home is simpler than physically attending school. However, I believe that learning online can be more challenging because students often miss the personal explanations that teachers provide during in-person classes. Without direct teacher support, students might struggle, and the sense of interaction that benefits learning is lost. In my opinion, the traditional school setting is crucial since it offers both guidance from teachers and opportunities for social interactions.

Not all students learn in the same way; while some may prefer solitary study, many need help from educators. For instance, my sister stays after school to receive extra assistance from her teachers, who break down complex topics and review mistakes made in tests. This personalized attention not only helps clarify difficult subjects but also builds a deeper understanding of the material. Similarly, socializing plays an essential role in learning—my brother enjoys playing sports at school and values the chance to interact with peers and adults who provide real-life insights. School is not just about academics; it is also about developing social skills and preparing for the future. Therefore, despite the appeal of online classes for those who prefer studying alone, I believe the benefits of face-to-face education far outweigh the convenience of learning from home.

In many states, the consumption of drugs is unlawful and you need permission to purchase them. Although alcohol is legal, you must be 21 years old or older to buy it. Carrying guns is legal but, like drugs and alcohol, requires permission and a minimum age. To drive, you must obtain a license, and you need to be 16 or older. If you choose to get your license at 16 years old, you must drive with a copilot who is older than you to ensure you have the necessary experience to drive alone.

Work: When you have a job, there are rules you must follow regarding schedules and duties. You have a specific schedule that tells you when to come to work and when to go home; this helps keep everything organized for your employers. If employees arrive at work whenever they want, it can affect the company. For example, if you are an accountant and the company needs you in the morning but you decide to come in the afternoon, your deviation from the schedule can create problems with the accounts, and it becomes your fault for not following the schedule. Moreover, you have specific duties based on your skills, which means you cannot unilaterally decide to do something different or risk being fired.

Society: You do not have the freedom to do everything you want in public. For example, you cannot burn a library simply because you think it is a brilliant idea; you cannot kick or hit people on the street just to make your friends laugh; and you cannot enter private property to pick a flower that you like. You cannot make such decisions in your life.

In conclusion, we cannot let people make their own decisions. I am not saying that people do not have the right to do or be something; I am saying that they cannot do everything they want. They need guidance from experts and authorities, especially minors who do not yet have the consciousness to know what is right or wrong.

It is essential for individuals to seek direction from experts and authorities when dealing with major aspects of life. Relying solely on one’s own instincts may lead a person to erroneously assume that their actions are correct, even when they go against established rules and guidelines.

Consider the laws that regulate behaviors such as drug and alcohol consumption, gun ownership, and driving. For instance, using drugs is illegal in many states unless you have the proper authorization, and while alcohol is legal, it can only be purchased by those who are 21 or older. Similarly, owning a gun is permitted only with the required permissions and age restrictions, and driving legally requires a license. In many regions, new drivers under the age of 16 must have an experienced adult accompany them. These rules are designed to protect individuals and ensure that only those who are fully aware of the responsibilities involved are allowed to participate.

The need for guidance is also evident in the workplace. Employees are expected to adhere to specific schedules and duties, which helps the business run smoothly. If someone were to choose their own timing without following these rules, it could disrupt operations. For example, an accountant who decides to work on their own schedule might create serious problems for a company that relies on timely financial information. In the workplace, even though one’s skills and expertise are valued, there is little room for making personal decisions that deviate from established procedures, as failure to comply can ultimately lead to dismissal.

In society, not every personal whim can be acted upon freely. One cannot simply decide to set fire to a library because it seems like a brilliant idea, nor is it acceptable to physically harm others for mere amusement. Entering private property to take something, like a flower, without permission is clearly not allowed. These examples show that without proper oversight, individual decisions could easily infringe on the rights and safety of others.

In summary, while people do have rights and freedoms, they must recognize the importance of expert and authoritative guidance on significant matters. This is especially true for minors, who lack the mature judgment needed to distinguish right from wrong.

Many schools now offer distance learning, which allows students to attend classes from their homes using online or video conferencing tools. I believe this option is beneficial, especially for those who have unusual schedules or extra responsibilities. For instance, some students work during the night, and attending regular classes early in the morning can disrupt their sleep and overall performance.

Take the example of a friend who works late shifts, sometimes from 5 p.m. to midnight. Despite his workload, he must wake up very early, around 5 a.m., to make it to school. This routine leaves him exhausted during his first classes. However, graduating from high school is crucial for him to secure a better future. Many high school students find themselves juggling work after school, and online classes could provide them with the flexibility they need. This flexibility can not only allow them more rest but might also help improve their academic results, as they would have more time to complete homework and prepare for tests.

Another situation involves many teenage girls who become pregnant and choose not to return to their regular schools. Pregnancy can lead to unwelcome judgments from others, making it difficult for them to continue in a traditional classroom setting. With distance learning, these young mothers have the opportunity to stay on track with their studies while caring for their babies at home. This mode of education provides a practical solution for completing high school, ensuring that they do not miss out on an education simply because of early motherhood.

Overall, offering distance learning is a promising idea as it supports students facing various challenges. By allowing them to study from home, this program helps them manage work, personal commitments, and other obstacles that might otherwise interfere with their education, ultimately leading to better outcomes for many students.

John Lubbock once stated that "your character will be what you yourself choose to make it." This quote raises concerns about how children often alter their personalities when they feel inadequate, burdened by their own thoughts. The personal traits we carry can sometimes override our true selves, suggesting that many individuals may lose control over who they become.

It is clear that the way others perceive our qualities can create insecurities, pushing us to change in an attempt to exceed our inherited identities from family or society. In today’s world, influences such as social media and the internet exert significant pressure, often guiding our behavior in directions that seem beyond our control. Despite this, it is important to seek out positive influences that align with our individual values, as shifts in societal perspectives are inevitable.

Furthermore, this change is not exclusive to one demographic; everyone is susceptible to external influences. Personally, I have experienced significant transformations since moving to Virginia, adapting to a lifestyle that many would consider typical. As we are bombarded with examples from various public figures—like rappers whose lyrics and actions shape our perceptions—there is a risk that these influences might lead us astray, especially for newcomers in a place like California where the entertainment industry has a powerful impact.

Both children and adults can be swayed by the ideas of others, often choosing paths that seem predetermined by external forces. Yet, I take pride in living in a world where, despite these challenges, we continue to shape our futures. Every year brings new trends, challenges such as wars, pollution, or health crises, all of which are amplified by sensational influences that might distort our understanding of danger.

In the end, it is this ongoing conversation with ourselves and our environment that propels us forward, even when we feel stuck.

Ralph Waldo Emerson once said, "To be yourself in a world that is constantly trying to make you something else is the greatest accomplishment." However, I disagree with this statement because true achievement comes not by allowing the world to shape you, but by taking command of it and pursuing your own path. To truly be yourself, you must make your own choices, act on your own desires, and resist letting external forces dictate your life.

Firstly, it is essential to remain true to who you are and to refuse to allow the world to decide for you. When you take charge of your own decisions, you avoid the risk of losing yourself and feeling exhausted by life. Relying on others to make choices for you can lead to regret and confusion, while choosing your own path brings satisfaction because you understand the reasons behind your decisions. Those who let others choose for them often end up feeling unfulfilled and lost.

Secondly, achieving success involves following your passions and not permitting the world to control your actions. If you seek to accomplish great things, you must embrace activities and careers that truly interest you. When you do what you love, work does not feel like a burden, and you are more likely to persist even when challenges arise. By focusing on your own interests, you ensure that your efforts are genuine and that your accomplishments are deeply personal rather than imposed by societal expectations.

In summary, the key to real success is maintaining your individuality and making your own choices instead of letting the world dictate your path. By doing so, you can better navigate life's challenges, decide what is right for you, and pursue a career or goal that truly resonates with your passions. Letting the world control your destiny may lead to dissatisfaction and regret; instead, assert your independence and show the world that you are in charge of your own future.

Later in the night, they start hearing noises but can’t tell where they’re coming from, so they scream “Mom, Dad!” again because the child thinks there is still a monster in the room, but the parents still insist that there are none. Later on, the child begins to think there is still a monster, so the child goes outside the room and notices that there is no monster—it was just their parent making noise to scare the child for fun.

I share Albert Einstein's view that imagination is even more significant than knowledge. When you learn, your mind doesn't just absorb facts—it also sparks creative ideas that help you understand and discover new information. Although there are moments when your imagination might lead you astray and confuse your thoughts, it often directs you to seek out or create the knowledge you need.

At times, however, knowledge can prove more reliable than imagination. For example, when faced with a challenging problem like that puzzling math question in a test, your well-established knowledge helps you navigate and solve it. Similarly, reading a book can enrich your vocabulary and ground your ideas in reality, showing that knowledge plays an essential role in practical situations.

Moreover, there are instances when both imagination and knowledge work hand in hand. Consider a situation where you have a vague idea of wanting to build something. Your imagination sparks various creative concepts, while your knowledge guides you on how to bring these ideas to life through careful planning and execution. This collaboration between creative thought and learned information enables you to achieve something remarkable.

Nevertheless, there can be downsides. Sometimes, excessive imagination might lead you to feel hopeless, or cause misunderstandings in social interactions. Imagining a negative outcome during play, for instance, might make a situation seem unfair and harm your friendships, even if your academic knowledge later allows you to perform well on a test. In such cases, boasting about success may result in losing a friend if you are insensitive.

Take, for example, a 16-year-old boy seeking employment. Even if he has some potential, his lack of focus on studying might prevent him from acquiring the necessary knowledge, making his job search more difficult compared to peers who have dedicated themselves to learning. This imbalance between imagination and knowledge can lead to serious consequences, such as financial difficulties or relying on friends for support, which might eventually result in a downward spiral.

Young children, in particular, display a remarkable ability to imagine without restrictions. At night, they might believe there is a monster in the closet, calling out for their parents. Despite the parents' assurances, the child's imagination can still create a lingering fear. Sometimes, even harmless teasing—like a parent making playful noises—can further blur the line between reality and imagination, showing just how powerful and unpredictable the human mind can be.

Technology enables us to complete many tasks without direct interaction with others. We can borrow books, shop, and play games all without speaking face-to-face. However, reducing human contact through technology has harmful effects on our lives. We have become overly reliant on technology, using it every moment, and in doing so, we risk losing our essential human qualities.

In the field of education, the problems become evident. Today, lessons are often delivered through online presentations, which can leave students without the personal guidance they need to fully understand their assignments. In my youth, teachers would explain assignments on the board and patiently go over the details again if confusion arose. That kind of teacher-student connection seems to vanish in our modern, tech-dominated classrooms. I still recall the times when my friends and I gathered in the school cafeteria to share our day; nowadays, lunch breaks are spent absorbed in our phones, with little conversation among peers.

The influence of technology extends even to our social and political spheres. With advanced technology fueling arms races and even nuclear conflicts, people are now more inclined to stay indoors, enjoying movies, books, and games provided by the digital world. This constant engagement has dulled our natural emotions and weakened our sense of community. I remember how, in the past, I would visit the library to pick up a book, rather than staying comfortably at home to order one online. Social outings where we could enjoy each other’s company have been replaced by solitary meals and online food orders, further eroding personal connections.

In the workplace, while technology can be helpful, it often serves as a major distraction. Employees can easily lose focus if a game or a news event catches their attention on their phones, which in turn decreases productivity. Such distractions may lead to job losses and the subsequent challenges of finding new employment and earning a living. In many instances, technology proves more harmful than beneficial.

Moreover, technology has contributed to an increase in accidents. For example, texting while driving causes a lack of attention on the road, often leading to collisions that result in severe consequences for everyone involved. A small moment of distraction can cost someone their life, leaving behind grieving families.

Overall, technology has a profoundly negative impact on our lives. It makes us less connected, more complacent, and even less human, stripping away the natural bonds formed through direct, personal interactions. By overrelying on technology, we risk losing the essence of what it means to truly connect with one another.

Success is a word we often hear, and everyone aspires to be successful in life.

The journey toward achievement begins at school, a vital and cherished stage of our lives. To make learning more engaging and enjoyable, schools and teachers often incorporate activities like educational role-plays, entertaining science experiments, and opportunities for students to play their favorite instruments.

Many talented actors, comedians, and performers we admire today once sat in the same classroom chairs we do now. They put in the effort, participated in school performances, and worked hard to hone their skills. Their stories show us that by participating in these activities, we too can progress toward success. Engaging in role-plays is not only enjoyable—it also helps build confidence when speaking in public and expressing ourselves. Moreover, making others smile through our performance brings immense joy.

In addition, advances in technology and science have led to new experiments each day, and there is no sign of this progress slowing down. This is why it's important for students to learn through hands-on experiments. By offering fun and safe projects—such as creating a rainbow in the air, mixing colors, or performing a disappearing coin trick—schools foster a greater interest and focus on science among students. This approach is vital, as today's learners are the leaders of tomorrow.

Every student possesses hidden talents, whether it be in music, art, sports, or other fields. Music, in particular, is one of the most prominent talents because it touches our hearts and sets our minds at ease. With its variety of moods—happy, sad, or even angry—music can evoke strong emotions. We encounter music everywhere, from television to music classes, and it allows us to express our feelings and feel lighter inside.

Ultimately, I believe that school is primarily a place for learning. When we find joy in every class and absorb new knowledge, we prepare ourselves for the challenges and rewards of life. School remains our most important resource in the quest for success.

Some schools now offer distance learning, allowing students to join classes from home via online platforms or video conferencing. In my view, this method does not provide the best environment for learning. Students at home may become easily distracted and fail to concentrate as much as they would if a teacher were physically present. Without direct supervision, they might not receive the attention needed when they require extra help.

Often, students dealing with personal challenges may not engage properly in online classes. They might skip the work assigned or simply search for answers without truly understanding the material, feeling that no one is watching. This lack of accountability can lead to a superficial grasp of the subject, and although they might manage to pass, their overall comprehension remains shallow. Furthermore, when students face significant issues in their lives, they miss out on the opportunity to interact with someone who can offer real support, like a teacher, coach, or counselor, which is more easily available in a traditional school setting.

Another issue with online classes is that they allow for dishonest practices, such as having someone else complete assignments. With the absence of a teacher's immediate guidance, students are more tempted to cheat rather than learning on their own. As a result, when it is time to complete tests on their own, they struggle to understand the subject. These problems are compounded by family issues that can distract students even more when they are studying from home.

The social aspect of school life is another important factor. Taking part in traditional classes helps students develop their interpersonal skills, which are crucial for future success. For instance, students involved in school sports not only learn teamwork but also form friendships that enrich their high school experience. Missing out on these opportunities may have long-term consequences, affecting their ability to communicate effectively in the real world.

In summary, I believe that distance learning does not meet the educational and social needs of students as well as traditional classroom settings do. The limited interaction with teachers and peers, combined with the potential for distractions and poor study habits at home, fails to provide the comprehensive support that students require. Schools should continue to promote in-person learning to ensure students receive both quality education and a well-rounded high school experience.

Winston Churchill once remarked that "success consists of going from failure to failure without loss of enthusiasm," a sentiment I strongly support. Although some people argue that constant failures show a lack of genius, I believe that as long as you remain passionate and determined, success will eventually follow.

A clear example of this idea is the story of AiDiSheng and his creation of the light bulb. Despite facing countless setbacks, he never wavered in his enthusiasm. Each failure brought him closer to his goal, ultimately leading to a breakthrough that changed history. This shows that if you remain focused and maintain your excitement, you can achieve your dreams, no matter how many obstacles come your way.

Moreover, it is important to remain bold and persistent. When faced with repeated failures, friends might discourage you, suggesting that your efforts are futile. However, giving up would mean losing the spark that drives you toward your goals. Trusting yourself and continuing to try, regardless of the criticism, is key.

In my view, genuine enthusiasm is not easily found. It often comes from a deep interest in something that captivates you—like playing video games for hours without noticing the passage of time. If you could bring that same level of passion to studying or any other challenging activity, success would be well within reach.

Failure itself is not the worst outcome; the real tragedy lies in abandoning your enthusiasm. If you believe in yourself and keep moving forward, even through repeated failures, success is ultimately attainable.

Many students eagerly look forward to summer vacation because it is one of the most enjoyable times of the year. During this season, they get the opportunity to spend quality time with family and friends. Although some teachers argue that a long break might cause students to forget what they have learned, I believe that summer is a very special period that allows everyone to reconnect with the people who matter the most.

Summer provides a rare chance for families to be together, especially when many parents work long hours from Monday to Saturday, and even sometimes on Sundays. These busy schedules often leave little room for quality time with loved ones. For me, summer vacation is a time filled with many positive experiences. I get to travel to different places and enjoy peaceful moments at home, and the opportunity to bond closely with my mom makes this season even more valuable. My mother is always there for me in both good and difficult times, offering advice and guiding me away from the mistakes she once made. Spending the summer together helps me improve in school, work, church, and many other aspects of my life.

My mother, who is an essential figure in my life, has always supported me and motivated me to succeed in all areas, including school. During summer, I also enjoy deepening my relationship with God, whose presence teaches me important life lessons. Two months of vacation are a welcome break after nine long months of schooling. The constant demands of homework and projects can sometimes be overwhelming, making the summer break a necessary period for mental rest and enjoyment with those we love.

Some educators claim that the long summer vacation hampers information retention, but I disagree. The lessons learned from class assignments, projects, and homework remain in our minds, forming the foundation of our knowledge. Another argument I oppose is the idea of a shorter, year-round school schedule with only a few weeks off in the summer. This kind of schedule would hardly allow time to relax and bond with family. I firmly believe that summer should be a time to enjoy life’s moments with parents, siblings, and extended family, not just a period of academic worry.

I remember a time when I was overwhelmed with schoolwork—homework, projects, and presentations took up most of my thoughts. When my family suggested spending time together, I hesitated because I felt too burdened by assignments. My uncle encouraged me by pointing out that it was important to take a break and enjoy family time. In hindsight, I realized that I missed out on precious moments that cannot be regained. It is important to balance education with family time, because the support of loved ones is invaluable.

Education is certainly important, as it helps us understand the world around us—from human nature to the mysteries of the solar system and the simple laws of nature, like water. The knowledge we gain can build a foundation for the future and even be shared with others in need. Ultimately, it comes down to setting priorities. When it’s time for school, focus on studies, and when it’s time for family, enjoy their company.

I have learned to balance my schedule: weekday mornings are dedicated to education, while weekends are reserved for spending time with my family and deepening my connection with God. This approach has allowed me to cherish the moments I have with my loved ones. Summer vacation is particularly meaningful for students whose parents are often away due to work commitments, providing them with more opportunities to finally be together.

In conclusion, summer vacation is not too long, and in fact, it is a welcome break that helps clear the mind and build stronger family bonds. Both students and teachers benefit from this time to refresh themselves, review what has been learned, and enjoy precious moments with family members. Enjoy your summer, and make the most of every moment with the people who matter most.

I believe that revising the cafeteria menu would be a positive change. At my school, some days the food is enjoyable, but more often it is not very appealing, and many students grow tired of eating the same dishes every week. This constant repetition contributes to widespread dissatisfaction with the available options.

I also feel that adjusting the prices on the menu could be beneficial. There are students who cannot afford lunch, and as a result, they often skip a meal despite the possibility of having nutritious and tasty options. Lowering the prices might allow everyone to enjoy a good meal without financial stress.

In addition to these changes, it would be helpful for everyone to know the daily menu in advance. Many students are curious about what will be served each day, so displaying a daily schedule or calendar at the cafeteria entrance could provide useful information and help them plan accordingly.

Another important improvement would be to extend the lunch break to one hour. This adjustment would give students more time to relax, interact with friends, and even spend a few minutes discussing school subjects with their teachers. A longer break could make lunchtime a more social and informative part of the day, benefiting both students and staff.

Overall, altering the cafeteria menu is a worthwhile idea because the majority of students are dissatisfied with the current food selection. For instance, in my school, the food is often subpar because there is little effort to change it, leaving many students unhappy. By modifying the menu, reducing prices, displaying the daily offerings, and lengthening the lunch period, the school could create a more welcoming and accessible dining experience for everyone.

His father worked in construction while his mother was busy taking care of the family and preparing everyone for school. In his community, many never had the chance to attend school at all, which made his opportunity even more significant.

His father had distanced himself from other people and became involved in dangerous groups. One day, while on his way to work, he encountered four men. Attempting to escape, he was caught too late; a gunshot wounded him critically, and he succumbed to his injuries before anyone could help.

My grandpa’s elder brother also faced a heartbreaking fate. After falling ill for two months, his condition worsened. Despite his intelligence and the way he helped my grandpa improve his reading and writing—earning him high grades at school—the illness proved too strong in an era and place where modern medicine was scarce and prohibitively expensive.
