I firmly believe that attending classes from home provides no advantages. I will explain three main reasons for this stance. First, students often learn very little during online sessions, especially toward the end of the term. Second, studying at home makes it easy for students to get distracted, so they rarely focus on the lesson. Lastly, face-to-face teaching in a classroom setting is far more effective and engaging.

To begin with, students tend to absorb less information when they are seated in front of a computer rather than in a classroom. In a home setting, assignments are often rushed through just to complete them, which means students miss out on truly understanding the material. This lack of engagement can lead to problems later when they are required to demonstrate their knowledge.

Moreover, the home environment is filled with distractions. When studying online, students have constant access to devices like cell phones, televisions, or even the same computer used for class, which can easily divert their attention. For instance, family members might interrupt or assign extra tasks, further reducing the time available for focused learning. In addition, the presence of electronic devices or even friends playing video games nearby can seriously undermine concentration.

Finally, the benefits of direct interaction in a classroom are undeniable. I appreciate the opportunity to discuss topics in person with teachers and classmates, as it not only deepens my understanding but also provides diverse perspectives. In a classroom, the clear communication of ideas aids in retaining information better, whereas lessons taken on a computer are often forgotten shortly after.

In conclusion, learning in a classroom where students can interact directly with teachers and peers is the best method for a thorough education. Classes conducted at home tend to result in missed content and poor academic performance. Additionally, the multitude of distractions available in a home setting only serves to divert attention away from the material. Focusing on in-person classes is key not only to academic success but also to developing essential social skills for life.

Being true to who you are in a society that constantly urges you to conform is a significant achievement. In today’s world, appearance often matters more than genuine personality. Many individuals feel compelled to present themselves in a way that does not reflect their true nature, and comments about personal style or behavior can quickly lead to frustration. This social pressure undermines individuality, making it a notable feat to maintain one’s authenticity.

We live in an environment where the opinions of others frequently take precedence over our own self-image. The constant focus on physical appearance drives many to abandon their true selves in order to fit in or meet external expectations. Choosing to embrace your unique qualities, regardless of others' judgments, is essential to staying true to who you are.

I fully agree with the idea that being oneself is a major accomplishment. Every day, we face the challenge of resisting societal pressures that demand we act or look a certain way just to please others. Instead of yielding to negative comments or trying to mimic an image that is not our own, it is important to stand firm in our individuality. Even though it is not easy in a world dominated by superficial evaluations, remaining authentic can lead to personal fulfillment and growth.

In conclusion, the path to embracing your individuality is filled with challenges. When we refuse to let stereotypes dictate our behavior and ignore the negative influence of others, we pave the way for a more genuine life. Being true to yourself is not only admirable but also essential, as it breaks down the barriers imposed by societal expectations and allows you to achieve a deeper sense of self-worth.

Such acts not only help strengthen personal relationships but may also encourage others to pay it forward. I have experienced this firsthand—when I offer a brief compliment, it brightens someone's day, and during times when I’m not feeling my best, the kindness of others lifts my spirits. Over time, you become known for your generous nature, which can lead to even more positive interactions and a lasting impact on those around you.

Furthermore, this ripple effect of kindness can uplift whole communities. Our world often feels tainted by negativity, but if people make a conscious effort to be nicer to one another, that change could spread quickly. For instance, when one person experiences the joy of being treated kindly, they are likely to extend that courtesy to others, creating a continuous cycle of goodwill. This phenomenon became evident in my own school experience. By consistently showing kindness, I became more visible among my peers, inspiring them to also be kind and supportive.

A simple compliment can turn someone’s entire day around, and the positive energy radiates outward to those nearby. I remember facing difficult times during my early teens, and the support and kindness I received from friends made a world of difference. When someone in need receives such kindness, it can lead to a happier, brighter outlook on life.

In conclusion, even the smallest act of kindness has the power to change someone's life by building personal reputations, transforming communities, and brightening individual days.

Some schools now provide the option for students to participate in classes remotely via online platforms or video conferencing. Many educators see this as an advantage, especially for those who are unable to attend in person due to health issues or other personal obstacles. However, while both home-based learning and traditional classroom attendance offer certain benefits, neither option is completely superior overall.

On one side, remote learning can be very helpful for students who face physical challenges or illnesses that make attending school difficult. For instance, a student who struggles with mobility issues due to arthritis might find it impossible to travel to a physical classroom. Similarly, some young learners may have parents who restrict their attendance because of health concerns. In such cases, online classes or video sessions with tutors offer a viable alternative, ensuring that these students still gain the education they need and can eventually earn a diploma. Additionally, for students who sometimes encounter conflicts or feel unsafe in a traditional school setting, home-based learning provides a peaceful environment where they can focus without disturbances.

On the other hand, remote education may not be as effective for students who are less motivated or lack the necessary support system at home. Without the direct supervision of a teacher, some students might find it easier to become distracted and struggle to keep up with their studies. This is particularly true for those learning a new language. For example, a non-native English speaker might benefit more from regular interactions in a classroom, where they are immersed in the language through constant practice with fellow students and teachers. As a student who has experienced both, I have found that the dynamic environment of a physical classroom, with its ample opportunities for practice and immediate feedback, greatly enhances my learning progress.

In summary, while studying from home offers important benefits, especially for students with health issues or those who experience difficulties in traditional school settings, it is not a perfect substitute for the comprehensive experience of attending school. Both methods contribute to education, but each has its own strengths and weaknesses. Ultimately, the choice depends on the individual needs of the student, and regardless of the setting, the goal remains the same: to learn and progress in life.

This essay discusses a proposal adopted by some companies to shift to a four-day work week while extending daily hours by two. I will share my perspective on whether this model should be introduced at my high school, exploring both its pros and cons, and recommending some steps that should be taken before any decision is made.

Imagine receiving a notice from your school explaining plans to reduce the school week to four days and lengthen each school day by two hours. I oppose this plan because it could negatively impact our high school rather than offering any benefits. One major issue is that the extended school day, which would last about ten hours, could lead to increased fatigue among students, potentially discouraging participation in after-school programs and activities. This situation is particularly problematic for juniors and seniors who often balance school with part-time jobs, as the longer hours might force many to quit their employment.

There are both advantages and disadvantages to implementing this schedule change. On the positive side, longer class periods might allow for more in-depth lessons and additional academic work during the school day, and the change might also help the school save on energy and other resources. However, the downsides are significant. Extended school hours could lead to the cancellation of extracurricular activities due to a lack of energy and interest, and students who juggle work may have to adjust their job schedules—or worse, quit their jobs entirely.

Before any school adopts this new approach, I believe it is essential for the school administration to take several preparatory steps. First, teachers and staff should meet to examine the proposal in detail. Next, a meeting should be arranged with parents, during which the concept would be clearly explained and discussed. A follow-up step could involve sending a detailed letter home that requires a parent's signature, indicating whether they support or oppose the changes. Only after these discussions and consultations should a final decision be made regarding the implementation.

To sum up, I do not support the introduction of a four-day school week with extended daily hours at my high school because it could harm rather than benefit our learning environment. The potential drawbacks—such as reduced participation in extracurricular programs, disruption to student jobs, and increased exhaustion—outweigh the benefits. I believe that our current schedule strikes a good balance by allowing time for academic work, sports, and other activities.

This essay explores the pros and cons of implementing a four-day school week, where each school day lasts ten hours. Although some argue that this system might help conserve energy and resources, I believe that extending the school day by two hours for most students creates more problems than it solves.

As a student, I find the idea of a longer weekend appealing, but I am not in favor of increasing daily school hours. Many students already struggle with an eight-hour day, which can lead to fatigue from long periods of sitting in class. Often, there are classmates who doze off due to heavy homework loads, part-time jobs, or after-school activities like sports. For them, adding another two hours in the classroom, just to gain an extra day off, seems like an unfavorable trade-off.

When we consider the claim about saving energy, the benefits do not add up. While reducing the number of school days might appear to cut down on energy usage, the extra time spent each day simply compensates for the loss of a full day. In effect, the additional two hours spread over four days equal the eight hours lost on the fifth day, meaning that overall energy consumption remains almost unchanged.

For example, one of my friends appreciates the four-day schedule because it offers him extra time to complete homework and spend time with his girlfriend. In contrast, my boyfriend, who loves studying, opposes the idea because he is involved in sports, requiring two hours of training after school, followed by a six-hour period that includes work and homework. His situation is not unique, as many students face similar challenges, balancing academic responsibilities with family and work obligations.

It is also important to consider the teachers. They, too, would have to conduct classes for extended periods, and like students, they are not immune to exhaustion. Teachers, being human, might find it difficult to maintain a high level of energy and engagement during a continuous ten-hour school day.

Based on these reasons, my school should not switch to this model. Decisions about changing the school schedule must consider the welfare of everyone involved—students, teachers, and administrative staff alike. While some businesses might successfully adapt to such a timetable, the unique demands of a high school setting, with its variety of activities and responsibilities, make this approach less suitable for us.

Every student should take part in at least one extracurricular activity because it offers numerous benefits both now and in the future. Research consistently reveals that individuals who remain physically active tend to enjoy better health and have a lower chance of disease.

Admissions officers often prefer well-rounded candidates who demonstrate the ability to balance academic work with other pursuits. A strong record of involvement suggests that a student can manage responsibilities effectively and shows a readiness for the challenges of higher education.

In conclusion, encouraging every student to engage in at least one extracurricular activity is a worthwhile policy. The benefits are evident in physical health, emotional well-being, and future academic opportunities. While it might not be every student's first choice, trying out different activities can lead to unexpected rewards both during high school and beyond.

I do not support extending the school day by an extra one and a half hours. Firstly, students already spend about eight hours at school engaged in classes and other activities, leaving them both physically and mentally tired. Adding more hours would only increase the exhaustion felt by children and adults alike.

Secondly, a longer school day means less time for the leisure activities that define childhood. After spending nearly ten hours in school, kids hardly have a chance to relax or enjoy free time. For instance, when you finish school, you're usually too tired to have fun and then must complete homework, which often takes several hours—making it nearly impossible to enjoy any outdoor activities, especially when it gets dark.

Furthermore, the additional homework often assigned during these extra hours means that students come home still burdened with work. For example, leaving school at 4:00 p.m. already leaves little energy, yet many still need to spend two or three additional hours on assignments. As a result, there’s little or no time to meet friends or participate in enjoyable activities.

Lastly, the extended schedule can interfere with other important commitments, such as appointments. Students might be forced to stay until 3:00 p.m. when they should be elsewhere, disrupting plans and personal time—even if early dismissal is an option, it reduces valuable learning time.

I understand that some believe longer school hours are intended to help us become smarter and achieve success in life. However, both students and adults need time for themselves as well. For all the reasons mentioned, I firmly disagree with increasing the school day.

I believe that judging someone solely by their first impression is unfair. It is important to take the time to understand a person rather than label them based on an initial encounter. For example, if someone appears tired and we quickly assume they are lazy, we may overlook the reasons behind their behavior and miss out on discovering their true personality.

Furthermore, I think that change is always possible because our mindset can be transformed over time. In the past, I was very shy and rarely engaged with others because I was afraid to speak up. However, as I became more comfortable with myself, I learned to break out of my shell and started introducing myself to new people without hesitation.

Technology plays a major role in our lives today and promises to become even more influential in the future. Humans naturally strive to improve their lives, seeking convenience and efficiency in everything they do. While some appreciate these advancements, others argue that technology diminishes personal interactions. They worry that people are increasingly avoiding face-to-face encounters in public spaces, preferring instead to remain in environments dominated by screens, and even reacting negatively when their concerns about technology are raised.

In earlier days, social interactions took place in the streets and public areas, without the aid of devices that now allow us to see and speak with friends on a small screen. This shift has led to a situation where people rarely leave their homes to socialize or enjoy the urban landscape, opting instead for virtual conversations with strangers. Some might claim that chatting online is no different from meeting someone on the street, but the risks are much higher online. There is a danger of encountering individuals with fake profiles who might steal personal information, unlike in real life where one can observe a person’s behavior before forming a connection.

During childhood, playing outside—in the streets, at a friend’s house, or in local parks—was a source of joy. Nowadays, however, technology has changed this dynamic. Video games, which once emerged as a novel form of entertainment, have now become a dominant pastime among children and teenagers. With just a device connected to a television, youngsters can play for hours, often choosing virtual worlds over outdoor activities, sports, or face-to-face interactions with friends. Conversations at school frequently revolve around these games, which can distract from studying and homework. In the past, when video game consoles first appeared, many children had to choose between buying the new gadget or simple pleasures like a treat or a visit to an amusement park. Today, however, the allure of technology keeps many young people indoors.

The widespread availability of technology has also brought about behavioral issues. When access to devices is limited or taken away, some children react with aggression. Such reactions have become increasingly common in households all over the world, with parents finding it difficult to manage their children’s dependency on digital entertainment. Experts suggest that kids become overly absorbed in a virtual world where they feel free to do as they please, and any attempt to disrupt this environment can lead to outbursts. This trend is not limited to younger children; teenagers too can become destructive, sometimes even damaging the expensive equipment provided by their parents.

While there are arguments that technology improves our lives by making everyday tasks simpler, its negative effects—such as reduced face-to-face interaction and behavioral issues among the young—indicate that we may be sacrificing important aspects of our humanity. Unless we find a way to balance its use, technology may continue to influence our society in ways that could be harmful in the long run.

Most students enjoy summer vacation, but some educators feel that students don't retain information as easily when they return in the fall and believe that summer break is too long. However, they should also consider the students' point of view and how the students feel about this. Educators shouldn't turn student breaks into a year-round school schedule; instead, there should be a 3–4 week break in the summer and a week off in both the spring and fall because students don't have as much time to spend with their families and most have responsibilities.

The first reason is that students don't spend enough time with their families. School takes up their time when they return home, and students come home every day to do their homework and get ready for the next day of school; some even have projects to work on. While they are focused on schoolwork, they sometimes forget about their parents, which can affect them because they don't share enough about what's going on in their lives. Educators feel that students' breaks are too short, and that is the first reason why student breaks shouldn't be turned into a year-round school schedule with no proper breaks.

Finally, the second reason is that most students also have responsibilities. Students have lives and things to do, and during summer, spring, and winter breaks, many try to help their parents and use their free time as they wish without the stress of homework and projects. Many students also believe that most of the information they learn at school is not valuable, which is why they forget much of it when they return. This is the final reason.

Although some people feel that summer break is too long and that students do not retain information as easily when they return in the fall, others believe otherwise. The fact remains that educators shouldn't implement a year-round school schedule without proper breaks, because this leaves students with less time to spend with their families and ignores their responsibilities. That is why summer, spring, and winter breaks should not be removed.

Many students look forward to summer vacation, although some educators argue that lengthy breaks negatively affect the retention of knowledge when school resumes in the fall. However, this perspective often overlooks the students’ own needs and experiences. Educators should not adopt a year-round school calendar that replaces the traditional extended summer break with only short recess periods—about three to four weeks in the summer and one week each in spring and autumn—since doing so would reduce valuable family time and ignore students’ other responsibilities.

Firstly, reducing the length of summer break limits the time students can spend with their families. When classes resume, many students find themselves caught up with homework, assignments, and projects, leaving little opportunity to share important moments at home. Without adequate family interaction, students might miss out on crucial emotional support and guidance, which can affect their overall well-being.

Secondly, students have lives outside of academics filled with various responsibilities. Their breaks serve as a period for relaxation and allow them to help out at home or pursue personal interests without the pressure of constant schoolwork. Many students feel that much of the content taught in school is quickly forgotten, suggesting that a shorter summer break does not significantly harm their learning and that the extra rest is essential for balancing their busy lives.

In summary, while some believe that a long summer vacation hinders academic retention, the evidence shows that modifying the schedule to a year-round system would undermine essential family time and student responsibilities. Maintaining a longer summer break, along with shorter spring and autumn breaks, respects the needs of students and supports their personal growth.

In the United States, many schools now offer the option for students to attend classes from home as a way to address issues such as bullying, especially in middle and high schools. Some students prefer staying at home to avoid the stressful environment of traditional classrooms. Despite these perceived benefits, learning from home can also lead to a decrease in academic engagement, as the structure of remote classes may not be as effective as in-person teaching. Although online or video-conference lessons allow students to relax and feel safe at home, they also make it easier for distractions to take over.

At home, students often find themselves sidetracked by smartphones and other digital devices. The lack of a structured environment makes it harder for them to remain focused, and extended time at home can lead to boredom and reduced productivity. For students who already struggle with concentration, the temptation to sleep during lessons or get caught up in non-academic activities increases, especially when they also have work obligations that leave them exhausted.

The challenges of maintaining concentration extend beyond distractions. Students who have difficulty paying attention in a classroom often find that the home setting only worsens their ability to stay engaged. The appeal of listening to music, playing games, or engaging with social media becomes a significant hurdle when trying to follow online lessons.

The traditional classroom environment has a natural flow where students benefit from direct interaction and immediate clarification from teachers. However, when lessons are delivered online, this dynamic is disrupted. Many students find it more difficult to comprehend complex topics without the face-to-face guidance they receive in-person, which can result in a weakened learning experience overall.

While schools believe that offering home-based classes can provide a more comfortable and secure environment for students—allowing extra time for homework and even more rest—this benefit is often overshadowed by the distractions of home life. The presence of family and the comfort of a familiar setting can sometimes lead to a lack of focus, preventing students from fully engaging with their studies.

In summary, although online classes from home are seen as a beneficial alternative by some, they frequently lead to reduced concentration and lower levels of learning. Distractions, whether from digital devices or the home environment in general, hinder the educational process and make it difficult for students to grasp the material, ultimately undermining the effectiveness of remote learning.

In recent years, many schools have begun offering remote learning options through online classes and video conferencing. I believe that these alternatives are extremely valuable because they create opportunities for students who struggle to attend traditional classes. For many students, personal circumstances, financial limitations, or other responsibilities make it challenging to follow a regular school schedule, and distance learning offers a practical solution.

Online classes in particular help students who want to complete their education but face obstacles such as work commitments or family obligations. Often, the need to support oneself or one’s family forces students to work, leaving little time for homework or studying. With the flexibility to attend classes from home at convenient times, these students can manage both work and education without sacrificing one for the other. This method also assists those who do not have a reliable support system nearby, allowing them to keep up with their studies while still meeting their financial needs.

Another useful method is video conferencing, which allows students to participate in real-time classes. This interactive format resembles a traditional classroom because students can see and communicate directly with their teachers. Immediate feedback is available when students have questions or need clarification, ensuring they do not fall behind in their studies. This real-time interaction helps bridge the gap between online and in-person learning.

One of the major advantages of these remote learning options is the ability to balance study with work and other personal activities. Furthermore, distance learning is not limited to young students; adults who wish to finish their high school education can also benefit. This inclusiveness means that anyone, regardless of their age or current situation, has the opportunity to earn a diploma.

With a growing number of teenagers and other learners at risk of leaving school due to a lack of options or motivation, offering remote learning provides a much-needed solution. It enables many who have previously dropped out or never participated to pursue a better future. In essence, when schools embrace distance learning, they not only eliminate excuses for not completing education but also open the door to improved opportunities and a brighter future for all learners.

Students who live far away or struggle with learning often find it difficult to succeed in traditional classes. Teachers worry about these students and try every method possible to support them. When principals noticed that grades were very low, they decided to seek a solution. A meeting was held, and it was suggested that students complete their assignments at home—a method known as Home School.

Home School is a program that allows students to work on homework, quizzes, assignments, and tests from home. Many students appreciate this approach because they feel it is easier than attending regular classes. For example, they can stay at home, have their lunch, watch TV, and still find enough time to finish their assignments.

However, some students do not favor Home School because they become bored at home. They miss out on making friends and receiving direct help with their schoolwork, which limits their access to important information. Often, students end up in Home School because their local area lacks proper schools, yet parents are determined to give their children the best education possible for a successful future.

If I were in charge of making this decision, I would advise students to attend regular school. Being in a traditional classroom offers better opportunities for success since students can interact with friends, collaborate on assignments, and receive more personalized guidance from teachers. Although Home School can be a useful program for academic success in some cases, regular school provides a stronger foundation for future achievements.

Allowing the use of cell phones during free periods would also make the school day more flexible and efficient.

Similarly, advice from parents or trusted mentors often encourages persistence in the face of challenges, which can instill lifelong resilience and a strong work ethic. Their guidance helps shape your understanding of right and wrong, much like sampling dishes from various chefs allows you to discover new flavors—each one potentially changing your perspective.

Ultimately, advice serves as a valuable tool to help you navigate through life. While not every opinion may align with your own views, considering diverse perspectives can empower you to become a more knowledgeable and well-rounded person. Taking in and reflecting on different viewpoints is essential to making informed, bold choices in the world we live in.

In my view, there are both advantages and drawbacks to allowing students to use their phones in school. On one hand, smartphones provide quick access to information and are easier to use than computers, which is beneficial because students are already accustomed to them. On the other hand, cell phones can cause distractions during lessons, leading students to focus on social media or texting instead of paying attention to their studies.

One major concern is that when phones are used in class, students tend to become less attentive and might even neglect their work. Schools already offer computers and libraries for research. Allowing phones can interrupt the learning process because students may spend too much time on non-educational activities while in class. For instance, even if a teacher permits them to use phones to look up helpful information, it is likely that many will misuse the opportunity for chatting with friends or browsing social media. Schools are meant to be spaces for focused learning and education.

Furthermore, modern teenagers have grown very attached to their devices. They often get frustrated if asked to surrender their phones in class. Students could benefit more from traditional methods, such as reading and engaging actively with their assignments, rather than quickly searching for answers online. There is a risk that during tests, students might use their phones to cheat instead of relying on their own knowledge. A possible solution could be to have teachers collect phones at the beginning of each class and return them once the lesson is over.

Despite these concerns, there are some positive aspects to using phones in school. They are generally faster and more user-friendly than computers, and they might help students seek additional information or discover new ways to understand difficult topics. Overall, while phones can offer conveniences like rapid research capabilities and efficient typing, they also risk undermining the classroom environment by distracting students. It seems that, although phones can support learning in certain contexts, their use in class often leads to distractions and even academic dishonesty.

Many urban areas have a curfew, set to encourage people to abide by a designated schedule while minimizing the chance of lawbreaking. Although some argue that curfews unfairly restrict young people’s freedom, these regulations help keep teenagers out of trouble by teaching them the importance of time management. Although some critics argue that curfews interfere with the lives of young people, in reality, they offer a window of opportunity for teenagers to complete their daily tasks in the early morning and evening. For instance, a 10 P.M. curfew not only ensures their safety but also helps them become more aware of time management. This arrangement reassures parents while giving teenagers the chance to prepare adequately for the coming school day or work period the next morning.

Is it beneficial to commend a student's work regardless of its quality? At first glance, rewarding effort seems positive, yet within education, offering praise without constructive feedback is problematic. Individuals naturally enjoy recognition, and repeated practice that is reinforced by positive feedback can indeed enhance performance. However, if the only response to a student's work is blanket praise—such as a constant “great job” or perfect grades—the incentive for further improvement diminishes. In such situations, learners may never develop the resilience required to handle criticism, which is crucial for personal and academic growth.

Consider the example of artists. Many creators recognize that their work is never perfect, and it is often the dissatisfaction with their own creations that pushes them to evolve and refine their skills. They value honest critiques over insincere praise because real progress depends on the ability to acknowledge and learn from mistakes. Similarly, students must learn to accept balanced feedback. In the real world, people will face critical assessments, and without prior experience in handling constructive criticism, students risk being unprepared for future challenges.

In summary, while positive reinforcement is important, it should always be accompanied by honest evaluations. A combination of commendation and constructive criticism is essential to motivate continuous improvement and prepare students for the inevitable criticisms they will encounter in life.

I believe that your character will be what you choose to make it. The decisions you make play a big role in who you become; for example, the people you hang out with, how you grew up and the household you were in, and your motivation—all contribute to building good character traits for the future.

The people you hang out with play a big role in your character because you can pick up many good and bad habits from them. They heavily influence what you do, and as the saying goes, "you are who you hang with." For example, if you spend time with people who do nothing but good, you are likely to adopt their behavior, whereas if you hang around with lazy individuals, you may also become lazy and unmotivated.

The way you grew up and the type of household you were in also have a significant impact on your character because that is the energy you are around all the time. For example, if your parents are constantly having problems at home, you might feel depressed or down, and that negative energy can even cause you to struggle in school. On the other hand, if your household is positive and everyone is happy, the constant good energy can make you a cheerful and optimistic person and help you succeed in school.

In my opinion, motivation is the most important part of building good character traits because having something to work for makes a big difference. If you are truly motivated, the past does not matter and you can become the best version of yourself—for example, if you are really motivated, you can become anything you want. Overcoming past challenges and family struggles can push you to work even harder, building lasting character traits along the way.

In conclusion, you create your character by choosing the people you hang out with, the household you live in, and the factors that drive your motivation. I do not believe you can be influenced beyond your control because you decide everything you do. For example, if you do not like your friends, change your social circle; if you do not like how things are going at home, consider living somewhere else. Everyone should know that nobody can or should control you, because ultimately, you are the one who makes your own choices.

I believe that who you become is largely determined by the decisions you make. The choices you make in life, such as the friends you associate with, the way you were raised, and the environment you live in, can significantly influence your character. Additionally, having strong motivation is essential because it drives you to develop positive traits.

The friends you choose to spend time with have a profound impact on you, as they can impart both positive and negative influences. There is some truth in the saying, "you are who you hang with." If you surround yourself with individuals who strive to do good, you are likely to adopt similar behaviors. Conversely, if your companions lead inactive or aimless lives, you might find yourself influenced to follow the same path.

Similarly, the environment in which you are raised plays a crucial role in shaping your personality. The atmosphere within your home can affect your emotional well-being and overall outlook on life. For instance, constantly witnessing conflict or sadness at home may leave you feeling down and even cause struggles in areas such as academics. On the other hand, growing up in a joyful, supportive household can foster a sense of happiness and positivity that benefits many aspects of your life.

Perhaps the most important factor in developing a strong character is motivation. When you are driven by clear goals and a passion for improvement, the difficulties of your past become challenges you can overcome. This determination can boost your self-esteem and help you work towards becoming the best version of yourself. Even when faced with adverse circumstances, the desire to achieve can lead you to develop admirable qualities that last a lifetime.

In the end, it is your responsibility to shape who you are. By choosing your friends wisely, cultivating a positive home life, and nurturing your own motivation, you have the power to direct the course of your life. Remember that while external factors may attempt to sway you, the ultimate control over your decisions and actions lies within you.

A current debate revolves around whether the energy-saving strategies used by some businesses—such as adopting a four-day work week with extended ten-hour days—should be applied to schools by lengthening the school day by two hours.

Many argue that this change would not be beneficial. They point out that increasing the daily schedule would mean that students, teachers, and staff need to spend more time at school, which could lead to fatigue. Moreover, even though classes would run for only four days, the daily hours would far exceed those in a typical five-day schedule. This extra time might also translate into additional requirements to meet graduation criteria, creating an even heavier workload. Critics suggest that schools could explore other energy-saving measures, such as shutting off unnecessary lights or ensuring proper ventilation by opening windows, rather than extending the school day.

I believe that extending the school day by two hours would be challenging for most students, especially since many have after-school jobs or other responsibilities that require their time. If classes run longer, it might conflict with these commitments. I also feel that using energy carefully and seeking input from those outside the school could lead to more effective ideas for conservation, rather than simply changing the school schedule.

In addition, a four-day school week with ten-hour days could make learning more strenuous. The extended daily hours might lead to exhaustion, reducing students' ability to absorb new material. There is also the potential issue of disrupted sleep patterns, with early wake-ups and late returns home. Despite the slight changes in scheduling, the total energy expended could be similar to a five-day week. Once tiredness sets in, the process of learning new concepts and units may become considerably more difficult for many.

In conclusion, determining the best approach requires open discussion and careful consideration of different opinions. It is important to recognize that some students require additional time to grasp new information. Given other straightforward methods to save energy, such as those mentioned earlier, extending the school day seems to impose unnecessary challenges.

Technology has come a long way over the years, and its progress has brought about many improvements in our daily lives. Some argue that this rapid advancement might be reducing our personal interactions, but I believe it has had a very positive influence on society. For instance, technology has revolutionized industries by enhancing the efficiency of how we build cars, airplanes, and even how restaurants operate today—imagine dining where tipping is no longer expected!

Even though advanced technology may replace some jobs, it remains one of our most valuable tools. Take the automobile industry as an example: companies now use robotic technology to produce vehicles. With highly sophisticated machines, a car can be assembled every ten minutes, which is astounding. Furthermore, the entire process of purchasing—from selecting a vehicle to acquiring spare parts—is streamlined online, eliminating the need for traditional customer service interactions. Near my local dealership, there is even a restaurant where they rely entirely on technology, offering a glimpse into how our daily routines have adapted.

In the world of dining, technology has completely transformed the experience. Ordering your favorite meal on a tablet speeds up the process and minimizes human error, ensuring that what you want is exactly what you get. Although this method reduces the number of staff interacting with customers, it offers benefits such as consistent service and the convenience of not having to worry about tips. Meanwhile, restaurant staff can focus on other important tasks unless the customer specifically needs assistance. This type of innovation is similar to what we see in large stores like Walmart, where technology has helped speed up checkout times significantly.

I have witnessed slow cash registers and incorrect change in traditional settings, which can be very frustrating. Self-checkout systems, however, have made the shopping experience much faster and more reliable. Even if these systems occasionally malfunction, they usually perform well, and it becomes normal not to see an employee manning the register. 

Ultimately, technology has improved our quality of life by streamlining processes and reducing stress. Imagine if companies like Ford had to hire millions of workers to manufacture a car in hours, or if a restaurant needed to manage a large staff with inconsistent service. The convenience and efficiency created by modern technology not only save us time but also make everyday tasks smoother.

I believe that the first impression can change for three reasons: your clothes and appearance do not reveal your true personality, the kind of person you are depends on truly knowing the person, and your idea about someone can change as you get to know them.

The majority of people classify a person based on how they look. What I believe is that your clothes and appearance do not show your real personality or the kind of person you really are.

Based on my short experience, getting to know a person takes time, and the first impression could be unfavorable in strong relationships or friendships. That's why I believe that who you are depends on knowing what kind of person you are.

Most of the strong friendships or relationships that I know began when the individuals were enemies or did not have a good first impression. However, over time, they had the privilege of getting to know the person and discovered a true kind of goodness in them.

To conclude, the first impression is a good way to present ourselves, but as we get to know the person, we find that the initial impression may not reflect who they truly are. That is why I believe that the first impression can change through knowing the person.

Some people argue that a person's character can be judged by their initial appearance, suggesting that the way someone dresses or presents themselves defines who they truly are. However, I contend that first impressions can be misleading for several reasons. Firstly, the way someone looks does not necessarily reflect their inner nature. It is by spending time with someone that we get to understand their true personality.

In my experience, truly knowing another person requires time. It is common to form a negative first impression, yet as we learn more about an individual, our perspective often changes dramatically. Many strong relationships have begun with misconceptions, only to grow into deep, meaningful connections once one gets to know the real person behind the surface.

Ultimately, while first impressions can serve as an initial introduction, they do not fully capture who someone is. Real understanding comes from extended interaction, which often reveals qualities that were not apparent at first glance.

When I was growing up, my parents always encouraged me to push past my limits. They believed that stepping outside of your comfort zone and striving for what seems impossible is essential for personal growth—unless you take the initiative yourself, nothing will change. I firmly agree with Emerson’s statement because only by challenging ourselves do we truly improve, develop our unique qualities, and ultimately achieve our dreams.

The saying "Practice makes perfect" is something we've all heard many times from loved ones. This is exactly what Emerson meant to convey: improvement is impossible without consistent practice. Personal growth also depends on hard work and dedication. I remember in middle school when I aspired to join the basketball team, despite not being very skilled at first. A close friend on the team offered to coach me if I committed to practicing each day. Thanks to regular practice before the tryouts, I managed to perform well and secure a spot on the team, proving that perseverance pays off.

My father once advised me that when it came time for college, I should choose a path that was not only ambitious but also unique. During my final year of high school, I decided to enroll in an online class to earn some college credit and experience a new learning format. Initially, it was challenging to study without the direct support of a teacher, but stepping out of my familiar routine helped me grow. After a couple of weeks, I started to adapt, and by the end of the course I had earned a B+, confirming that exploration beyond one's comfort zone can lead to success.

The efforts we put into conquering new challenges eventually yield valuable rewards. My experience with the online class, which began with fear, transformed into confidence, and now I believe I can handle any similar challenge. It is clear that either working alone or with someone else, getting rid of routine limitations and embracing new experiences pushes us to achieve greater things.

Some might argue that change is unnecessary for growth, but I disagree. Most people cannot truly learn or adjust unless they experiment with something different. Even failing to master something can provide the insights needed to differentiate between right and wrong.

In conclusion, if you work diligently and dare to step out of your comfort zone to explore new possibilities, you will continuously improve and reach new heights in life.

A positive attitude is fundamental for achieving success. Every action you take, no matter how trivial it may seem, requires belief in yourself; without confidence, even the smallest effort can lead to failure. However, experiencing failure should not be seen as entirely negative. It is through our mistakes that we learn and grow, preparing us for future challenges. When we face setbacks, we acquire a better understanding of our obstacles, allowing us to return with a new mindset, improved strategy, and enhanced determination—all resulting from what many label as "failure."

One might wonder why anyone would allow failure to occur when success is within reach. The answer lies in the reality that simply going through the motions without full commitment will not bring the desired outcome. In today’s competitive world, giving anything less than your full effort often means falling short while many others press forward. This is exactly where a positive attitude becomes critical. When you believe in your value and are willing to put forth 100% effort, you remove the barriers that might otherwise hold you back.

With self-assurance and a proactive, positive mindset, you will relentlessly pursue your goals regardless of who may oppose you, what critics might say, or the challenges along the way. This determination is the true key to success.

I do not support the idea of students attending classes via videoconference or from home. In my view, this online learning format often leads students to become disengaged, causing them to doze off or neglect completing their assignments. Based on my own experiences as a student, I believe that these issues can seriously impact academic progress.

One major concern is that students might delay participating, repeatedly promising to join later until they eventually decide that the online sessions are unimportant. This procrastination or complete avoidance may lead them to opt for outdoor activities or distractions from friends and family, rather than focusing on their studies.

Another significant issue is that students can easily fall asleep during online classes. Unlike in a traditional classroom where a teacher can immediately intervene, online environments do not provide the same level of supervision, making it difficult to ensure that everyone is engaged and awake.

Finally, there is the risk that students will not complete their work properly. Even if they log in, there is no guarantee they are the ones performing the assignments. They might ask someone else to complete their work or even pay for assistance. While some argue that learning from home saves time on getting ready for school and can be more convenient, many students benefit more from in-person interactions where teachers can offer direct guidance and explain concepts more clearly.

Overall, I strongly disagree with the practice of home-based education, as it tends to reduce motivation, accountability, and effective learning among students.

Maintaining a positive outlook can significantly improve your overall success in life. A good attitude not only makes social interactions smoother but also opens many doors, such as career opportunities and personal growth. In fact, there are two key reasons why having a positive outlook is so beneficial: it helps you earn respect from others and makes tasks like finding a job much easier.

Firstly, people are more inclined to appreciate and get along with someone who consistently shows respect and kindness. When you treat others with consideration, they are likely to return that respect, which helps build strong, mutually beneficial relationships. This is especially important during job interviews. A person who demonstrates a good attitude is far more likely to impress an employer than someone who comes off as negative or disrespectful.

Secondly, the respect you earn from those around you directly contributes to your success. When people respect you, they are less likely to deliberately undermine your efforts. Instead, they tend to support you, which can play a pivotal role in reaching your goals. In contrast, a negative attitude can often lead to a cycle of disrespect and missed opportunities, making it much harder to thrive in both personal and professional life.

Lastly, when it comes to opportunities like landing a job or getting accepted into a good college, a positive attitude is invaluable. Employers and admissions officers are more inclined to favor individuals who display confidence, optimism, and a cooperative spirit. On the other hand, a negative demeanor might result in rejection, regardless of your skills or qualifications.

In conclusion, maintaining a positive attitude not only makes you more likable and respected but also boosts your chances of success in various aspects of life. Whether you are seeking career advancement or nurturing personal relationships, a good attitude is a key ingredient in achieving your aspirations.

Deciding to specialize in a career at a young age can be considered a positive step for students. The school environment offers them a chance to discover various fields, allowing them to build experience and knowledge early on. While some may argue that young people already face many responsibilities—such as work or family duties—it is important to note that early career commitment can lead to long-term benefits.

One of the main advantages of choosing a career path during high school is that it prepares students for the demands of their future profession. By concentrating on a field they are passionate about, young individuals have the opportunity to practice essential skills on a daily basis. This continuous engagement not only enhances their learning but also builds their confidence when it comes to presenting their accumulated knowledge in a professional setting later on.

Moreover, in some societies it is expected that high school students identify their area of expertise. This early specialization enables them to understand their strengths and interests, making it easier to decide whether they are suited for a particular career. Knowing exactly what they want to become can lead to a greater focus on personal dreams and long-term goals, reducing the uncertainty many people experience as they transition into adulthood.

Another significant benefit is the chance to explore elective activities and practical work opportunities provided by schools. In many countries, students are often restricted to theoretical subjects and have limited options to gain practical experience. In contrast, opportunities to work during summer breaks or after school hours allow these young learners to gain hands-on experience in their chosen fields, ensuring they are better prepared than those who do not receive such exposure.

In conclusion, committing to a career at an early age is advantageous not only for the individuals themselves but also for society as a whole. Early career specialization helps students develop their skills, focus on their passions, and ultimately excel in the job market.

Life is composed of different stages that shape who we become, and growing up plays a crucial role in this process. From the moment we are born, we enter a cycle that includes childhood, adolescence, adulthood, and eventually old age. Each phase teaches us valuable lessons about responsibilities and independence—lessons that are essential for preparing for the future.

I agree with the idea that facing life’s challenges head-on is more effective than taking an easy route. This belief stems from the understanding that success comes from personal effort rather than relying on someone else to provide it. When you take control of your own earnings and make decisions that affect your life, you are forced to learn and grow in ways that truly prepare you for the future.

My personal experience supports this view. As a child, I quickly learned to handle daily responsibilities, such as cleaning up after myself and getting ready for school on time. As I grew older, I began small jobs which allowed me to earn money, and these early experiences helped me understand how to plan for a better future. They also taught me the importance of having a clear vision and a strong dream, not only for myself but also for my loved ones.

In conclusion, life is best enjoyed when you fully embrace its challenges and opportunities. By recognizing what you want to achieve and planning accordingly, you build a sense of independence and freedom that can lead to a fulfilling life, free from unnecessary constraints.

Extending the school day by an extra two hours seems unnecessary, especially since students already manage a busy schedule filled with work, sports, or club activities. Many students favor a four-day school week because it leaves them with more free time, even though it might mean less time at school overall if extra hours are added. While a shorter school week provides the advantage of a three-day weekend throughout the school year, which can be used for homework or catching up on missed work, the extended day could be more harmful than helpful.

Longer school hours can lead to reduced concentration and a decline in interest during lessons, with students feeling tired and likely to lose focus or even fall asleep. If I attended a school with an extra two-hour extension every day, I would probably struggle to remain attentive during classes, which could ultimately hinder my academic progress. On the other hand, some benefits include the possibility of shortening the school year, allowing more time for longer holiday breaks such as spring break.

Ultimately, while a shorter week offers a chance for additional relaxation and personal time, the idea of prolonging each day by two hours seems to undermine the potential advantages of the four-day school week. In my view, the drawbacks of decreased concentration and overall fatigue outweigh the potential benefits of extra instructional time, making the proposal of a longer school day less appealing.

I firmly believe that changing the world is within our reach, even though many claim it is impossible. Often, the only barrier is the mindset we carry, and by shifting our perspective, we can truly transform our environment. It is essential for individuals to adjust their views and recognize the significant impact even small changes can have. While some argue that altering our ways is too difficult or ineffective, I am convinced that personal transformation is the first step toward a larger collective change.

Every day, we face numerous challenges, such as global warming, that remind us that our lives are not as secure as we might hope. The effects of climate change emphasize the need for immediate action, and waiting for someone else to take the initiative is not a viable option. We have been contributing to environmental harm for too long, but the time to act is now. The change we aspire to begins with personal accountability and evolves into a shared responsibility. Just as a tree undergoes seasonal shifts, we too can evolve and make a difference. By improving ourselves, we can inspire others to view the world more clearly and encourage positive transformation across communities and nations.

I also believe that the power to change lies with every single one of us. Despite the challenges and setbacks that life may bring, I refuse to give up on the possibility of making a difference. It is important to understand that mistakes are not failures but valuable lessons that pave the way for success. In my view, a simple act of changing one’s behavior can have a ripple effect on society, leading to broader change over time. The key is to push forward, even when the task seems overwhelming, because each small improvement can accumulate into a significant impact.

On a personal level, I am driven by the desire to become a better person and to help others do the same. I aspire to be kind, responsible, and punctual, knowing that by setting a positive example, I might encourage others to adopt these traits too. One of my passions is technology, and I dream of integrating innovation into everyday life. For example, I envision creating a personal robot to assist with household tasks, despite the risks that technology might bring. Along with this, I hope to design a smartphone powered by solar energy, a sustainable solution in a world where energy resources are limited. These projects represent just a few ideas that reinforce my belief that no challenge is insurmountable if we are willing to try.

In every setting—from home and school to the broader community—our behavior defines the potential for change. Teachers and mentors play a crucial role in guiding us towards a better future by encouraging healthy habits and responsible actions. I imagine a world where even a simple video or animation shared on social media can inspire positive change, connecting people from diverse backgrounds with a common goal. When individuals see that even a small step can lead to a better life, the momentum of change grows stronger and reaches across borders.

Ultimately, every effort, no matter how small, contributes to a greater transformation. Learning from mistakes and continuously pushing ourselves forward is the real key to turning the impossible into the possible. Life is fleeting, and each day offers a new chance to make a positive impact. It starts with each of us taking responsibility, being persistent, and never losing sight of the vision of a better world. The journey might be challenging, but together, our collective actions can and will create lasting change.

Teaching young children in elementary schools is a truly rewarding experience. It provides the opportunity to meet a variety of people, interact with students, and even engage with their families. The chance to share knowledge with young minds is both enjoyable and nostalgic, often reminding us of our own school days.

Delivering lessons to elementary students is not only fun but also brings back memories from our childhood. You might choose a particular subject to focus on, whether it's math, science, or any other area, and see the joy in the students as they grasp new concepts. For instance, when a student confidently explains what a noun is, it can evoke memories of simpler times spent learning in school. Although teaching these young learners might present some challenges, it becomes easier as you build a connection with them. Discovering their different interests and learning styles adds an element of excitement to every session.

Working with elementary school students also gives you a glimpse into school life beyond the classroom. You have the opportunity to meet many teachers, interact with school principals, and sometimes even encounter relatives or friends from your own past. Being in this environment can boost your own learning skills by reminding you of the techniques and methods used in early learning.

Elementary school experiences often ignite memories of our own days when we made friends with classmates from 4th and 5th grades. The students may sometimes challenge you with questions about subjects like math, science, or English, making each class a dynamic learning opportunity. Fun games and interactive activities are integral to the daily routine, motivating the children to work hard and complete their assignments with enthusiasm.

In essence, teaching in elementary schools is not only a pleasure but also a beneficial experience that helps prepare these young students for a successful future. By sharing your knowledge and passion, you contribute significantly to their ongoing learning journey while also rekindling your own fond memories of childhood.

In my view, each individual should have the freedom to pursue what they love, rather than being pushed into careers or studies chosen by society or parental influence. When someone is deeply interested in a particular field—whether it’s a profession, language, writing, discovery, or healing—the enthusiasm they feel when learning something new can fuel them to overcome obstacles and reach great heights.

Take my personal experience as an example. I have always been drawn to business studies and have pursued them throughout my educational journey in my home country. However, when I moved to the United States, my family and others around me insisted that I needed to become a nurse. Lacking the internal passion for nursing, I felt an overwhelming sense of doubt and discouragement about the future. Had I been working in a field that truly inspired me, I believe I would have embraced the challenges rather than feeling weighed down by them.

In light of this, I stand in opposition to Emerson’s statement. Some may argue that our surroundings shape who we become, but I believe that no one can force you to go against your true interests unless you allow it. It is essential to take a stand, confidently express your choices, and pursue the path that ignites your passion. Achieving success in the domain you love is one of life’s greatest honors.

I believe that working in a group is very beneficial. When you collaborate with others, time seems to pass quickly and the experience is much more enjoyable. By working together, you can support each other and even form new friendships, which is something you might miss when working alone. Solo work tends to feel slow, and without anyone to talk to, it can become dull quickly. Also, when working as a team, if you encounter something difficult, a group member might provide a new perspective that helps you understand the task better. For instance, if a project is divided among four people, each member can handle a section of the work and explain it, and if one person forgets something, others can pitch in to clarify. In contrast, if you have to handle a presentation alone, explaining everything on your own can be overwhelming, and there is no one to offer assistance if you get stuck or confused. Thus, I believe that working with a group of people is a much better approach.

Learning from home is not as effective as attending classes in school. When students are at school, they have access to a wide range of learning options, which can be very helpful when they encounter difficulties. In a classroom setting, teachers can provide immediate guidance and explain concepts multiple times if necessary. On the other hand, while distance learning is useful for those who are sick or have specific reasons preventing them from attending school, it still relies on the student’s own motivation to keep up with their studies.

Distance learning at home can sometimes help students focus better since classes are available at any time and there might be fewer distractions. Additionally, students may benefit from the flexibility to listen to the lessons and engage in activities they prefer. However, even though some schools offer the option of taking classes online, attending school physically remains very important. Being in a school environment increases the opportunities to interact with teachers and classmates, which is essential for better understanding and graduating alongside peers. In my view, attending school provides more chances to learn and achieve personal goals than distance learning or video conferencing can offer.

Some students argue that having a long summer vacation is beneficial because it gives them ample free time to enjoy with their friends. However, I believe that a year-round school system is a better alternative. In this model, students would have a short summer break of about 3-4 weeks, a longer break during the winter, and another week off in both spring and autumn. This approach would help prevent boredom from constantly studying and provide students with regular opportunities to recharge.

The idea behind a long summer break is that students, especially those whose parents live abroad, might take the time to visit their home countries and reconnect with family and friends. While this is true, a lengthy summer vacation can also lead to a loss of focus and an increase in the workload when school resumes.

In my view, spreading out breaks throughout the year helps reduce the stress of continuous study and prevents the negative effects of long holidays, such as laziness and difficulty readjusting to academic routines. Shorter, more frequent breaks can do wonders for maintaining a steady learning rhythm without overwhelming students.

Overall, I firmly support the idea of transitioning to a year-round school calendar, which includes a brief summer vacation along with breaks in winter, spring, and fall, as it fosters a more balanced and less stressful educational experience.

Some schools allow cell phones in class for educational purposes, but I believe that these devices should not be used during lessons. The main reasons are that students already spend too much time on their phones, the devices are often used for non-educational activities, and they tend to distract from learning.

Many students spend most of their day on their phones, which leads them to pay less attention during classes. Although phones can be useful for looking up information, the frequent usage during lessons means that students miss out on key learning opportunities. When tests or quizzes come around, their lack of concentration can prevent them from recalling important information.

Moreover, cell phones are often used for activities unrelated to schoolwork. Students might text friends, play games, watch videos, or listen to music instead of focusing on the teacher's instructions. In some cases, they even use their devices to record videos or take photos for social media, sometimes targeting others in a harmful way.

Some argue that cell phones can be a helpful tool for completing homework, projects, or when assistance is needed with a subject. However, the constant temptation to check apps or engage in face-to-face interactions undermines their academic use. This distraction often results in unfinished classwork and can have a negative impact on grades.

In conclusion, although cell phones are sometimes used for learning in the classroom, they often detract from students' educational experiences. The distractions they create, combined with the tendency to use them for non-academic activities, suggest that they should not be allowed during class time.

Some individuals believe in self-reliance, meaning that each person should trust their own instincts and judgment when making decisions about life. For these people, learning to appreciate what they have plays an important role in their everyday lives.

Many people attach great importance to material possessions like clothing, shoes, and phones, as well as close relationships with family and friends. They show that by taking care of these items, they reinforce their belief in earning and valuing their belongings. For instance, if someone spends a hundred dollars on a pair of shoes, they are more likely to be careful with them and avoid letting them get dirty. Similarly, when expensive shoes from popular brands are damaged, it is not just a loss of an item but a blow to personal pride and the sense of hard work that went into saving up for them.

This idea also applies to people who engage in physical work or spend time outdoors. In those cases, it may be wiser to choose less expensive footwear so that the item does not become a constant worry. Spending only a modest amount can ensure that the focus remains on working hard and appreciating what has been earned, rather than stressing over expensive possessions.

For teenagers entering the workforce, learning to earn their money rather than expecting expensive items can be a crucial life lesson. When young people understand the value of money and the effort behind earning it, they tend to take better care of their belongings and become more responsible. This way of thinking reinforces self-reliance and encourages a balanced approach to consumer choices.

Personally, I practice self-reliance by saving money for what I truly need. I understand the value of saving and investing in what matters. For example, when I gave a friend a pair of airpods for Christmas, I knew the gift represented more than just its price. It was a token of the time and effort I put into earning that money, and it made the gesture even more meaningful. Such experiences remind me that appreciating something you have worked hard for creates lasting bonds and a deeper sense of gratitude.

Ultimately, self-reliance is about both trusting your own judgment and learning to value your hard-earned possessions and relationships. This approach leads to a more responsible and fulfilling life, where each item and each bond carries a meaning rooted in personal effort and care.

For instance, when I was a child living with my grandmother, she always advised me not to start smoking when I reached my early teens, explaining that cigarettes could ruin one’s health. Another important influence in my life occurred when I moved to the United States. At first, I struggled with English, but by reading books at home and dedicating my free time, I gradually improved my language skills. Listening carefully in class and paying attention to my teachers’ explanations further boosted my confidence in speaking English.

Along with my soccer dreams, I have other goals. I plan to complete high school in the coming year and start working to help support my family. I want to earn money for my personal needs, paying for college and even saving up for a car. All these experiences and goals show how influential guidance and determination can be in shaping a positive future.

Even if you have one hundred low goals, you cannot say, “one hundred low goals equal a high goal” because a high goal can lead to success; even if you pursue one hundred low goals, it is almost impossible to become successful.

It is very important to have high goals in our lives to be great people; by pursuing high goals, you can excel in anything, whereas by pursuing low goals, you can never be successful.

To start, it is very important to have high goals to be a great person. For example, Keanu Reeves, a successful actor, is a great person who shows that money is not the most important aspect of life. Sometimes a high goal is not always about having money; it can also be a personal goal.

Next, by setting a high goal you can excel in anything. For example, Kobe Bryant, one of the NBA’s greatest players, became the best in basketball because he wanted to be the best. You are not an anomaly; if you work for yourself, you can be the best at anything.

Finally, by pursuing low goals you can never be successful. For example, someone with low goals can never learn from his mistakes; furthermore, that person can never grow. However, if you want to become successful, you need to find something you feel passionate about and work for it.

High goals can be hard—even impossible—to reach, but we must never give up; when you say to yourself “I can do it,” you take the first step on the path to success.

Many individuals set goals for themselves, but there is a clear difference between those who aim high and those who settle for easier, more modest targets. While ambitious objectives demand a great deal of effort and perseverance, lowering your sights simply to make things easier is not the path to true success. No matter how many small goals you achieve, they rarely add up to the kind of accomplishment that comes from pursuing a challenging, high-reaching dream.

Pursuing high aspirations is essential for personal growth and becoming a remarkable person. Consider figures like Keanu Reeves, who, despite his success in acting, has shown that true achievement isn’t measured solely by wealth. His life demonstrates that personal fulfillment and greatness often come from setting and working towards lofty goals rather than accumulating material riches.

Furthermore, aiming high can empower you to excel in any area of your life. Take Kobe Bryant, one of the greatest players in basketball, who became the best largely because he set his sights on that goal and worked relentlessly to achieve it. His dedication reminds us that if you commit to a high standard, you can overcome obstacles and reach extraordinary heights.

On the contrary, choosing easier, low ambitions may hinder growth and learning. Without the challenge of high aspirations, there is little opportunity to learn from mistakes and develop the resilience needed for substantial success. If you want to truly better yourself, it is vital to identify something that ignites your passion and drive, and then strive relentlessly towards that dream.

In the end, although striving for high goals can feel overwhelming at times, it is important not to give up. Believing in yourself and your ability to overcome challenges is the first step towards a truly successful and fulfilling life.

Many people underestimate the value of constantly expanding their knowledge. Many seem content with what they already know, unaware that the little pieces of wisdom they accumulate can add up to something far greater.
